Yet he still wasn't sure. Taking in a living creature meant taking responsibility, and wasn't he... someone who had been abandoned himself?

What right or ability did he have—

A slight weight settled on his shoulder. The chubby bird flew over, tilting its head as if observing him.

Song Yu’s jawline was somewhat sharp and lean. In his pitch-black, dark eyes, subtle ripples appeared like reflections on a calm lake, mirroring the image of a tiny bird.

"It likes you."

His junior fellow student spoke up once more.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Who asked you! I said, who asked you!*

The bird spun its head around, short beak snapping open and shut, looking as though it was about to spout a barrage of curses.

The junior student mimicked in advance, "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp."

The young man even whistled at the end.

The bird was about to explode with rage. Its feathers puffed up, and it hopped twice on the shoulder, determined to take flight and peck that guy's face off.

However, Song Yu cupped his hands gently and caught him once again.

"..."

Bai Linlin was set down onto the kitchen island. Song Yu’s face was somewhat pale, but he still explained word by word:

"I won't be able to raise you well."

"I don't understand the habits of birds. Doing this would be irresponsible."

Song Yu felt his head spinning with dizziness. He was ill to begin with, and the blood vessels in his fingers throbbed with continuous, sharp pricks of pain.

Until a tiny, soft claw reached out and pressed against his hand.

Bai Linlin looked up at him.

*Intense eye contact engaged.*

The junior student found it amusing and reached out to flick the bird away. But in less than two seconds, the bird hopped right back, furiously chirping a few times in his direction.

Song Yu froze.

Qi Siyang raised a eyebrow, watching his junior classmate flick the bird away a second time. Although the bird was so angry its feathers puffed up like a pom-pom, it still obstinately scrambled right back onto Song Yu’s hand.

"Haha, it really likes you."

Bai Linlin was instantly struck with awkwardness.

"..."

Puffed up for half a day, only to end up looking completely pathetic.

Yet perhaps that single sentence truly took effect. Afterward, Song Yu said nothing more and saw the two guests out.

Bai Linlin stood proudly on the youth's shoulder, leisurely preening his feathers. *Victory in this battle!*

Night fell like still water. The sconce light by the kitchen island was turned on, casting a warm, atmospheric yellow glow.

It just so happened that the bird was standing right behind the light, casting a massive, moving shadow on the wall that looked immensely "majestic."

"Chirp chirp?"

Song Yu didn't know what he was contemplating. He lowered his head and sent a text message, instructing the cleaning auntie not to come over tonight.

He walked into the kitchen. The little bird on his shoulder was actually somewhat heavy—a solid weight. Occasionally, he could feel it tilting its head, sizing him up.

It was a very subtle, peculiar sensation.

Song Yu had lived alone for a long time. His personal space usually contained only himself, but now... an extra bird had entered it.

And it seemed to like him?

Song Yu’s face remained pale, his eyes pitch-black like concentrated ink. He suffered from mild somatization symptoms, yet right now, for some unknown reason, he didn't take his medicine right away.

Instead, he walked over to the cabinet, pulled out a small dish, and filled it with bird food.

This was all he knew how to do...

Did this count as raising it?

No, it didn't.

Song Yu stared blankly at the objects on the counter. His mind was in disarray, filled with chaotic, overlapping memories colliding in his head.

*"Little Song, your mother is pregnant again. Could you not call over these next few days?"*

*"You know it’s not very convenient."*

...

*"Song Yu, I don't have time to bother with you. It’s not like I gave birth to you. Go find your mother."*

*"Whose phone call was that? Yangyang was asking for you today."*

*"Aw, sweetie, home from school? Let Daddy give you a hug."*

These voices belonged to men and women alike—sometimes sharp and cruel, sometimes gentle and loving. They were like a collection of mask-wearing faceless dolls, constantly devouring his sanity.

"Chirp chirp?"

Song Yu snapped out of it. His fingers were ice-cold as he abruptly pulled away from the hallucinations. A faint itch tickled his cheek, and he turned his head to look.

A round, fluffy bird head was gentle nudging against him.

Song Yu raised his hand slightly. The bird’s round head tilted, peering at him for a moment before extending a bird leg to step firmly onto the "artificial perch" of his hand.

The bird food in the dish was new, pressed into tiny, high-quality pellets with virtually no dust or crumbs.

Bai Linlin was placed back on the counter. A quiet silence settled over him. *Do I really have to eat this?*

He tilted his head to glance up at the youth.

As usual, Song Yu lacked any dramatic expression, but at this close distance, the marks on his wrist were exceptionally clear—looking as though they had been carved by an artist's precision blade...

Bai Linlin couldn't help feeling a wave of worry.

A bird couldn't just leave like this.

A bird possessed a sense of social responsibility.

He pondered for a moment and decided that taking a few superficial bites would be fine. Thus, he leaned down and took a small nibble.

*Smack smack smack.*

Bai Linlin felt it tasted a bit like oatmeal mixed with a hint of fresh grass—surprisingly pleasant and addictive.

He took another peck.

Song Yu watched with lowered eyes, seemingly letting out a quiet sigh of relief, though his brows knitted slightly. He kept feeling as if he had forgotten something.

However, it was already getting quite late.

Intending to make do with a few slices of bread, Song Yu walked over to the refrigerator, raised his arm, and pulled open the door.

He stood there, frozen.

Inside was nothing short of total chaos. Every single sheet of plastic wrap had been poked open into ragged shreds. It wasn't just the bowl of braised meat that had been targeted; carrots and baby bok choy had bite marks, and even the plastic caps of ordinary beverage bottles had neat little notches gnawed into them.

"..."

chunks.chineseText:
第5章

卧室。

白粼粼被握着，鸟腿垂着，偶尔试图探头去看宋郁的手机屏幕，但还是看不太清。

好像是聊天软件。

师弟：[胡萝卜和青菜？那还好吧，它居然能撬开……]

宋郁坐在书桌的椅子上，指缝里还捻着那根被鸟充当装饰物的“纸条”，面色仍然有些困惑。

他的空闲时间消失了。

全部被一个小动物给占据了，但他本人其实并不能完全适应。

放生……不现实。

宋郁：[它可能吃了卤肉。]

对面迅速回复：

师弟：[不可能，鹦鹉顶多是叨两口玩一玩，不会吃的，那香辛料很多。]

师弟：[没什么事，你把冰箱门关紧就可以了。]

宋郁没有话要说了，修长的手指传来点湿润的感觉，少年抬眸一看，鸟正在专心致志地叨。

白粼粼：“……”

鸟松开了，黑松石一般的鸟眼看了过来。

但或许是因为眼睛是在两侧，白粼粼习惯于歪头观察宋郁。

这个姿势，显得很睿智。

“你是怎么打开的呢……”

宋郁有些出神地道，他换了家居服，锁骨若隐若现的，少年的青春气息尽显无遗，那根纸条在手指内侧卷了下。

大约一个小时后。

鸟被赶出了卧室。

宋郁其实是买了个笼子的，空间很大，但白粼粼压根不进，他没有什么经验，觉得可能是小鸟觉得闭塞。

那索性外面的空间都是它的。

别墅里的窗户全部封好了，没有飞出去的可能性。

白粼粼站在卧室门口外头，一阵沉默，觉得不行，在地板上蹦跶了两下。

问题一：别墅里好像只有宋郁一个人，那如果自己要做一些事，必须要依靠“人”。

问题二：“人”把“鸟”关出去了。

“……”

其实这是有些戏剧化的，一般宠物夜里是有笼养的，但有的主人为了确保自己爱宠的自由，选择给自己买了笼子，然后周遭趴着无数个猫猫和狗狗。

白粼粼压根不想去那个豪华鸟笼，他只想打游戏，很想，这是社畜下班之后的唯一爱好了。

电子竞技，谁与争锋！

于是乎，鸟站在门口，深沉地望着门把手，扑棱翅膀飞了上去。

开始往下“墩墩”。

具体表现在，一只圆滚滚的“小鸡”在上下用力踩门把手。

与此同时，宋郁在洗澡，温热的水流划过高挺的鼻梁，黑色的瞳仁里面没有什么光彩，只是看着暗沉沉的。

不过就在抬手拿毛巾擦头发的时候，听到了熟悉的细细簌簌的动静。

浴室门是磨砂制的，门口有一坨小小的身影，大摇大摆地叨了几下门。

鸟头一探一探的，似乎是很好奇。

宋郁蹙了蹙眉，索性直接拉开门了，浴室里的雾气也随之四处逃窜。

白粼粼被这阵开门的风给带的有些不稳，有一滴水落下，翅膀给弄湿了。

欸，洗澡。

他也想洗。

宋郁衣着完整，发梢沾水，只是附身蹲下，面无表情地伸过去了手。

鸟很满意地站上去了。

宋郁也不知道自己怎么了，或许是白天事情太多，他也有些烦躁，开始自动合理化。

鸟可能就是比较聪明的，冰箱门都可以打开，一个门有什么所谓。

这很正常。

别的鸟估计也会。

对，是这样。

宋郁抬手带着鸟回到了书桌那里，伸手靠着桌面，沉甸甸的小鸟挪动了下，他甚至能感受到爪子包裹手指的感觉，大约挪了几下位置。

下来了。

白粼粼伸展了下翅膀，估计是被打湿了点，整个鸟蓬松了起来。

像个毛球。

宋郁垂眸看了一眼，再度脑海成像：

[毛绒钥匙扣]

现在已经晚上八点半了，四月份的天气不算太热，窗户外面的树叶晃来晃去的，倒是十分静谧。

白粼粼在书桌上站着，看着宋郁抬手吃药，还注意到了对方撇过来的目光，淡淡的。

其实是有点：你在看我？

白粼粼可是光明正大地看的，现在他可是鸟了，切，衣服都不用穿。

爽得很。

宋郁果然没有再赶他，只是拉开椅子，开了电脑。

白粼粼：！！

鸟腿此刻走得很快，立马飞到了宋郁的肩头，准备去看开机密码。

[20070506]

白粼粼一下子就记住了，心里美滋滋，他还复习了下上次的支付密码：

[******]

好好好。

宋郁其实在输完密码就没有在动作，因为肩头站着只小鸟，他不太能分辨这是否是那位师弟说的“喜欢”。

但，不排斥。

爪子的存在感其实很强，稍微挪动一下，他就能想象到圆滚滚的“甜筒”在调整站姿。

比如现在。

宋郁面无表情，只有握着鼠标的手指微微动了下。

鸟的确在调整姿势，还时不时地张开翅膀，似乎是在梳理打湿的羽毛。

又蓬了一个度。

宋郁不知道自己在干什么。

“啾啾啾啾？”

白粼粼歪头看了过去，爪子往里面踩了踩，找了个合适位置窝好了，很是不解。

[玩游戏呀。]

宋郁回了下神，随便打开了个MOBA游戏，不过在等待匹配的时候，他察觉到肩头的一些动作。

爪子似乎往前伸了。

“……”

他在分心，甚至角色差点被一个蹲草的敌人杀了，不过好在丝血跑了。

“啾啾！”

宋郁唇角是平直的，眼皮垂着，一边操作，一边走神。

鸟腿往前一伸，它直接坐下了。

毛绒绒的。

宋郁操作的手指都停了。

不出所料，屏幕黑了。

白粼粼震惊，这在干什么，这在干什么？

死了，兄弟你怎么死了？

“啾啾啾啾啾啾！”

宋郁感觉肩头热热的，同时，也吵吵的，或许是吃了药的缘故，夜里竟然没有那么难熬。

打游戏到了十一点。

把把都是胜方mvp，宋郁面色很平静，输赢不重要，只是排解时间而已。

他本来是要起身的，但是肩头的小鸟似乎睡着了，一动不动。

宋郁坐在椅子上，没有再动过。

深夜了。

他的视线落在了桌面的那本书上，或许是心念一动，拿了过来，动作很轻。

封皮被啃出来一个条。

宋郁垂眸随便看了看教辅，都是再基础不过的知识，没什么好看的。

也就在这时，肩头一轻。

鸟迷迷瞪瞪地栽了下来，但本能地扑棱翅膀和伸爪子，半道把“人”的睡衣扣子给弄开了，在对方的锁骨上划出了一道痕迹。

宋郁抬手接住了。

白粼粼困死了，最后一个朦胧的记忆是被放进了一个四四方方的纸巾盒里。

-

四月天气，南市风景如画。

宋郁一大早就在打电话，掌心躺着一只两脚朝天、一动不动的鸟，宛若是……死了。

手机那边传来安慰的声音。

齐思扬：“应该不会……身体是热的吗？”

宋郁垂眸看着鸟，指腹碰了下那滑滑的肉色短喙，随即又滑到鸟头那里，摸了下。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 5

In the bedroom.

Bai Linlin was being held in a loose hand, bird legs dangling, occasionally trying to crane his neck to peek at Song Yu's phone screen, though he still couldn't see clearly.

It looked like a messaging app.

Junior Student: [Carrots and greens? That’s not too bad then. I can't believe it actually managed to pry those open...]

Song Yu sat in his desk chair, still twirling the strip of paper the bird had used as a decorative accessory between his fingers. His expression remained somewhat perplexed.

His free time had vanished.

It was entirely occupied by a tiny animal, but he himself hadn't fully adjusted to it.

Releasing it into the wild... wasn't realistic.

Song Yu: [It might have eaten some braised meat.]

A swift reply came from the other side:

Junior Student: [Impossible. At most, a parrot would peck at it a couple of times for fun. It won't actually eat it—the spices are way too heavy.]

Junior Student: [It's fine, just make sure you shut the fridge door tightly.]

Song Yu had nothing left to say. A sensation of dampness touched his slender fingers. The youth looked up; the bird was currently pecking at his skin with deep focus.

Bai Linlin: "..."

The bird let go, its obsidian-like eyes staring back.

However, perhaps because its eyes were positioned on the sides of its head, Bai Linlin was accustomed to tilting his head sideways to observe Song Yu.

This posture made him look exceptionally "profound."

"Just how did you open it..." Song Yu murmured, somewhat lost in thought. He had changed into loungewear, his collarbone subtly visible, exuding the undeniable youthfulness of a teenage boy. The paper strip curled gently against the inside of his finger.

About an hour later.

The bird was ushered out of the bedroom.

Song Yu had actually bought a cage—a very spacious one—but Bai Linlin refused to set foot inside. Lacking experience, Song Yu assumed the bird felt claustrophobic.

So, he simply left the entire outer space for the bird to roam.

All the windows in the villa were securely sealed; there was zero chance of it flying away.

Bai Linlin stood outside the bedroom door in a moment of heavy silence. *This won't do,* he thought, hopping twice on the floor.

Problem one: Song Yu seemed to be the only person living in this villa. If he wanted to accomplish anything, he had to rely on a "human."

Problem two: The "human" had locked the "bird" outside.

"..."

In truth, this situation was rather comical. Normally, pets were caged at night. Yet some owners, in order to guarantee their beloved pets' absolute freedom, chose to buy a cage for themselves while letting swarms of cats and dogs lounge around outside.

Bai Linlin had no interest whatsoever in entering that luxurious bird cage. He just wanted to play video games—he desperately wanted to. That was a corporate slave’s sole source of joy after off-duty hours!

*Esports! Who dares challenge me!*

Thus, the bird stood at the doorway, staring profoundly at the door handle before flapping its wings and flying upward.

He began to "stomp" downward.

Specifically, a chubby little "chick" was frantically using all its weight to trample the door handle up and down.

Meanwhile, Song Yu was taking a shower. Warm streams of water washed over his high-bridged nose. There was little brightness in his dark pupils, looking only gloomy and muted.

However, just as he reached out to grab a towel to dry his hair, he caught the familiar sound of faint rustling.

The bathroom door was made of frosted glass. A tiny shadow lurked outside the door, brazenly pecking against the glass a few times.

The bird’s head bobbed back and forth, seemingly filled with curiosity.

Song Yu knitted his brows. He simply pulled open the door, allowing the dense steam inside the bathroom to scatter and escape into the hallway.

Bai Linlin was knocked slightly off balance by the gust of wind from the opening door. A stray drop of water landed on him, wetting his wing.

*Ayy, taking a shower.*

*He wanted to take one too.*

Song Yu was fully dressed, though water dripped from the ends of his hair. He merely crouched down and extended his hand without any expression.

The bird hopped on with great satisfaction.

Song Yu didn't know what was wrong with him. Perhaps because too many things had happened today, he felt an underlying restlessness and began automatically rationalizing everything.

*The bird is probably just unusually smart. If it can open a refrigerator door, what’s a bedroom door?*

*This is completely normal.*

*Other birds can probably do it too.*

*Yes, that's it.*

Song Yu lifted his hand and brought the bird back to the desk. Leaning his hand against the desk surface, he felt the heavy little bird shift its weight. He could even feel the sensation of tiny claws wrapping around his fingers as it repositioned itself a few times.

It stepped down.

Bai Linlin stretched his wings. Since they were slightly wet, his entire feathered body puffed out completely.

He looked like a ball of fluff.

Song Yu lowered his eyes to steal a glance, an image automatically forming in his mind once more:

[A fluffy keychain.]

It was already eight-thirty in the evening. The April weather wasn't too hot, and the leaves outside the window swayed gently in the wind, creating a peaceful silence.

Bai Linlin stood on the desk, watching Song Yu reach out to take his medicine. He even noticed the youth darting a subtle glance toward him—cool and indifferent.

It was almost as if asking: *What are you staring at?*

Bai Linlin watched completely openly. *I'm a bird now! Hmph, I don't even need to wear clothes.*

*Feels great.*

Sure enough, Song Yu didn't kick him out again. He simply pulled out his chair and turned on the computer.

Bai Linlin: *!!*

His little bird legs moved with lightning speed, instantly flying up onto Song Yu's shoulder to get a clear view of the login password.

[20070506]

Bai Linlin memorized it in an instant, feeling giddy inside. He even mentally reviewed the payment password from last time:

[******]

*Nice, nice, nice.*

Song Yu didn't make any further movements after entering the password. With a small bird perched on his shoulder, he couldn't quite tell if this was the "liking" his junior student had mentioned.

However, he didn't dislike it.

The presence of the claws was surprisingly distinct. Whenever it shifted slightly, he could envision the plump "ice cream cone" adjusting its posture.

Just like right now.

Song Yu remained expressionless, his fingers merely twitching slightly on the mouse.

The bird was indeed adjusting its stance, occasionally spreading its wings as if preening its damp feathers.

It puffed up another degree wider.

Song Yu didn't know what he was doing.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp?"

Bai Linlin tilted his head to look over, stepping his claws inward to find a comfortable position to nestle down, looking utterly baffled.

*Play the game already!*

Song Yu snapped out of his reverie and randomly opened a MOBA game. However, while waiting for the match to queue, he noticed movement on his shoulder.

The claws seemed to be reaching forward.

"..."

He was distracted. His character was nearly ambushed and killed by an enemy hiding in the bushes, but fortunately, he managed to escape with a sliver of health.

"Chirp chirp!"

The corners of Song Yu’s lips remained straight, his eyelids drooping. He operated the controls while letting his mind wander.

The bird extended its legs forward and sat straight down.

A ball of fluff.

Song Yu’s operating fingers came to a complete halt.

Unsurprisingly, the screen turned black.

Bai Linlin was stunned. *What are you doing? What on earth are you doing?!*

*You died! Brother, how did you die?!*

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

Song Yu felt a warmth on his shoulder, accompanied by a very noisy chatter. Perhaps due to the effects of the medicine, the night didn't seem quite so agonizing.

He played games until eleven o'clock.

Every single match ended with him as the winning team's MVP. Song Yu’s expression remained serene; winning or losing didn't matter, as it was merely a way to pass the time.

He had intended to stand up, but the little bird on his shoulder seemed to have fallen fast asleep, completely motionless.

Song Yu sat in his chair, not moving an inch further.

It was late into the night.

His gaze fell upon a book on the desk. On a sudden whim, he reached out and picked it up with extremely gentle movements.

A strip had been gnawed off the cover.

Song Yu lowered his eyes and casually skimmed through the supplementary study guide. It was all the most basic knowledge—nothing worth looking closely at.

Right at that moment, the weight on his shoulder suddenly lightened.

Dazed with sleep, the bird lost its balance and tumbled off. Instinctively flapping its wings and stretching out its claws, it accidentally ripped open the youth's pajama button mid-fall, leaving a fine scratch mark across his collarbone.

Song Yu raised his hand and caught it just in time.

Bai Linlin was dead tired. His last hazy memory was being placed inside a square tissue box.

***

In April, the scenery of Nanshi was as picturesque as a painting.

Early in the morning, Song Yu was on the phone while holding a bird lying flat on its back with its legs sticking up in the palm of his hand, completely motionless—looking for all the world as if... it were dead.

A comforting voice came from the phone.

Qi Siyang: "It shouldn't be... Is its body warm?"

Song Yu lowered his gaze to the bird. The tip of his finger touched its smooth, flesh-colored short beak before sliding up to its head, giving it a gentle stroke.

chunks.chineseText:
“热的。”他同电话里的人说道。

对面的人似乎是沉默了一会，最后给出了比较专业的解释：

“那应该就是在睡觉，但是说实话，和尚鹦鹉这个品种，仰躺睡姿并不常见，除非从小养到大……”

“而且它应该很警觉才是，你都把它拿出来了，那照理说该醒了，啧……”

齐思扬觉得离谱，但最后发现一句也解释不了，什么神鸟？

宋郁垂眸等了一会，直到指腹传来一阵刺痛，小鸟叨了他一口。

“它醒了。”

电话就此中断。

齐思扬在工位上坐着，整个人都有些反应不过来，他回顾了下本科所学的知识，仍然不是很懂宋郁所口述的现象。

摇都摇不醒？

鹦鹉？

他觉得还是很奇怪，不过顺道同自己老师发了个邮件，说了下近期的项目进度以及宋郁的……近况。

与此同时。

白粼粼整个鸟都很困，站在宋郁的肩头张了张喙，肉色的小舌头往外伸了伸，然后收回，翅膀也合了合。

像是打哈欠。

宋郁在洗漱，神色淡淡的，但是抬眼看镜子的时候，还是把目光偏移了下。

鸟羽毛蓬松，站得稳稳当当。

鸟眼都还眯着。

宋郁尽管没什么反应，但还是避开了弯腰的动作，眼皮微微垂着，能感受到隔着布料的爪子挪动。

白粼粼执意不走路，一路都在人身上小憩，直到他被一把握了起来，挪到了餐桌上，上面放着一盘鸟粮。

宋郁就站在旁边，垂眸看着他。

有些时候仿佛不需要说话。

鸟仰头。

人抬手把盘子挪了过去。

鸟歪了下头，觉得还是敷衍一下，点了点头，示意自己知道了。

宋郁再度怔住了，不过或许是昨日已经有了经验，没在因为这件事去联系齐思扬。

说不定这个品种的小鸟都是这么聪慧的。

很正常，会点头怎么了？

理所应当。

白粼粼站上了盘子的边边，抬头看了下宋郁，为了符合鸟设，叨了几口鸟粮。

对方果然放心了许多，背着书包就走了。

白粼粼想了想，扑棱翅膀下地，很是兢兢业业地送了送人。

等到玄关门关上的时候。

一秒，两秒。

鸟鬼鬼祟祟，飞到了一楼窗户那里，确保对方真的走了之后。

“啾啾啾啾啾！！！”

[耶耶耶耶耶耶。]

白粼粼从善如流地飞到厨房，开始一段美食寻觅，尾羽微微上翘，圆滚滚的身子被冰箱夹住了也浑然不觉。

不知道过了多久，门口那里有密码输入的声音，钟点工阿姨提着新鲜的蔬菜就上门了。

路上还有几名健身的邻居打招呼。

“张姨又过来了啊？”

“啊是。”

“也是辛苦你了，那孩子也是可怜……”

作者有话说：

是的，每个人都将知道宋郁的支付密码
chunks.englishText:
"It's warm," he told the person on the phone.

The person on the other end fell silent for a moment before finally offering a relatively professional explanation:

"Then it should just be sleeping. But to be honest, for Quaker parrots, sleeping flat on their backs isn't very common unless they've been hand-raised since they were tiny chicks..."

"Besides, it should be very vigilant. You've picked it up and brought it out, so logically speaking, it should have woken up by now. Tsk..."

Qi Siyang felt it was utterly absurd, but in the end, he realized he couldn't explain a single thing. What kind of miracle bird was this?

Song Yu lowered his eyes and waited for a moment until a sharp prick of pain touched his fingertip—the little bird had taken a light nip at him.

"It's awake."

The call ended right there.

Qi Siyang sat at his workstation, feeling entirely unable to process the situation. He reviewed the knowledge he had learned during his undergraduate studies, yet he still couldn't quite comprehend the phenomenon Song Yu had described.

Couldn't even be shaken awake?

A parrot?

He still found it incredibly strange. However, he took the opportunity to send an email to his professor, reporting on the recent project progress as well as Song Yu's... current condition.

Meanwhile.

Bai Linlin was exhausted as a bird. Standing on Song Yu's shoulder, he opened his beak, stretched out his tiny flesh-colored tongue, retracted it, and folded his wings back.

It looked remarkably like a yawn.

Song Yu was washing up. His expression was flat, but when he raised his eyes to look into the mirror, his gaze drifted to the side.

The bird's feathers were puffed up fluffy, standing perfectly steady.

Its bird eyes were still half-squinted shut.

Even though Song Yu showed no visible emotion, he deliberately avoided bending over. With his eyelids slightly lowered, he could feel the tiny claws moving through the fabric of his shirt.

Bai Linlin stubbornly refused to walk, taking little naps on the human's body the entire way until he was gently cupped in a hand and moved onto the dining table, where a dish of bird food was placed.

Song Yu stood right beside him, looking down at him.

Sometimes, words felt completely unnecessary.

The bird looked up.

The human raised his hand and pushed the dish a little closer.

The bird tilted his head, deciding he should at least play along. He nodded his head once to signal that he understood.

Song Yu froze again. However, perhaps because he had already gained experience from yesterday, he didn't contact Qi Siyang over this.

*Perhaps birds of this species are simply this intelligent.*

*It's completely normal. What's so strange about a bird knowing how to nod?*

*It makes perfect sense.*

Bai Linlin stepped onto the edge of the dish, looked up at Song Yu, and took a few pecks at the bird food to stay in character.

Seeing this, the other party visibly relaxed quite a bit. Shoulder-slinging his backpack, he turned and left.

Bai Linlin pondered for a moment before flapping his wings down to the floor, dutifully seeing the youth off to the door.

The moment the entrance door shut tight.

One second, two seconds.

Acting sly and sneaky, the bird flew over to the first-floor window. Once he confirmed that the human had truly departed—

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!!!"

*[Yessssssssss!]*

Bai Linlin smoothly glided into the kitchen to begin a grand quest for delicious food, his tail feathers perking up slightly. He didn't care in the slightest even when his chubby little body got squeezed in the refrigerator door.

An unknown amount of time passed before the sound of a password being entered sounded from the entrance. The hourly maid, Auntie Zhang, stepped inside carrying a bag of fresh vegetables.

On her way in, she had exchanged greetings with a few neighbors who were out exercising.

"Auntie Zhang, heading over again?"

"Ah, yes."

"Must be tough on you. That child is so pitiful as well..."

***
**Author's Note:**
Yes, every single person will end up knowing Song Yu's payment password.

chunks.chineseText:
第6章

阿姨进门之后就把买来的新鲜蔬菜放到了桌上，准备去给做几个三明治，顺带也去预热了烤箱。

厨房里一阵阵的香气。

不过就在这时，阿姨口袋里的手机嗡嗡震动了起来，对面似乎是个中年男人。

“是，先生，我知道。”

“小宋也就上次去见他母亲了，最近没有再去过。”

“好，好，我知道了。”

白粼粼站在吊灯上面，鸟头往下垂着，非常严谨地观察新的“人”。

阿姨挂了电话后就叹了口气，但还是很利索地忙活了起来，但就在打开冰箱的时候，微微怔了下。

里面乱糟糟的，蔬菜胡萝卜也有一些坑坑洼洼的印记。

白粼粼活动了下鸟腿，短喙上还有点酸奶的痕迹，不过很快被咂巴干净了。

继续观察。

阿姨还没有进行下一步动作，又一个电话过来了，这次对面是宋郁。

“张姨，我给您发过消息了，您不用过来给我做饭。”

电话那边的声音很是冷淡，但还是保持了礼貌与客气。

但阿姨也有些为难，只是解释道，“我、我看到了，但是，先生那边……不好交代。”

别墅的智能门锁有密钥，宋父即使在国外，也可以授权管理。

那边沉默了一会。

宋郁几乎有些烦躁，“那我回来。”

白粼粼只能听出来个大概，他站在吊灯上，需要往下探探鸟头。

大抵是阿姨一直在道歉，说做完饭就会离开，同时也在劝说：

“小宋好好上课，是我的错，这、这我家里实在是缺钱，这份工作我暂时没办法不做，你请假的话，校方那里肯定要联系先生的，还是不要……”

白粼粼听着就窒息。

什么乱七八糟的。

后面不知道具体说了什么，但很快阿姨语气就变了，开始四处张望。

“是吗？哎呀，我没见到它呀。”

妇人更内疚了，在厨房里走来走去，甚至开始准备的去客厅那里找。

白粼粼本来是低头看着的，为了跟随目标移动，鸟头转得有点费劲，只能调整一下爪子，但这个古董吊灯实在是叮叮咣咣的。

刚一挪动，那阿姨就愣愣地抬头看了过来：

“小宋，找到了。”

十分钟后——

宋郁的手机屏幕里出现了一个鸟头，圆滚滚的，似乎是站在餐桌上，短喙张了张，似乎是打了哈欠。

这还是阿姨费了好些功夫哄下来的，一开始是用鸟粮，但压根不管用，最后是用得带回来的熟切火腿。

但白粼粼一口没有叨到，一个庞大的手机摄像头就对了过来。

对面的阿姨很是热络地对准小鸟，非常实心实意地夸赞：

“欸，这长得，真好看真好看。”

“小鸟小鸟，看镜头。”

“你主人在看你噢。”

白粼粼一时半会有点鸟脸泛红，这怎么和哄小孩一样？

阿姨还特地把摄像头给反转了下，用手当成小支架，给鸟去看屏幕里的主人。

宋郁倚靠在栏杆上，周遭没有人，好像是天台，额发有些微微吹起，眉眼在日光下显得尤为出众。

“……”

白粼粼不知道说什么，思来想去，对着人“啾啾”了几声。

手机摄像是有畸变的，鸟头圆滚滚占据了整个屏幕，短喙一张一合的，像是贴到“人”的脸上一样。

宋郁面无表情，但截了图。

这个视频通话，其实还是阿姨说的话比较多。

“取名字了吗？小宋。”

“还没有。”

“那要取个名字的，小动物也是家里的一份子，哎呀哎呀，真好。”

阿姨其实是很欣慰的，这孩子她也照顾半年了，对宋家的事也是知道一二的，了解内情之后很难不会心疼。

小鸟好，小鸟可以陪陪小宋。

白粼粼在餐桌上站着板板正正的，一开始有点无聊，不过后来看着屏幕里的宋郁，不知道怎么了，叨了一口。

“……”

少年垂眸看着，眉眼平和。

白粼粼歪了歪鸟头，又叨了一口。

“……”

最后还是上课铃响了结束了这场“无聊”的互动，阿姨在准备拿起来手机在说几句的时候，鸟往前走了走，探头探脑的。

“小宋中午吃什么？阿姨提前做好。”

“好好，你放心，我没有开门窗，小鸟很安全的。”

……

白粼粼瞅准时机，扑棱翅膀飞了过去，叨了下手机屏幕。

正好按到挂断键上。

阿姨又是一阵惊叹，连连夸了鸟好多句，一时半会甚至做饭都给忘了。

白粼粼非常矜持地又展示了自己的才艺，在桌子上飞了一圈，完美落地。

“小鸟，你好会飞呀！”

“来来来，阿姨给你拍照，发给我们小宋。”

白粼粼的虚荣心得到了极大的膨胀，不当人之后，世界都美好了起来。

-

大约三十分钟后。

阿姨认真查阅手机，给鸟切了一个指甲盖大的苹果肉，顺带把刚刚拍的图片都传给了宋郁。

她是不担心那孩子的学习的。

虽然生病了，但好像年年都是第一。

适当放松下也是好的。

白粼粼叼起来苹果认真地炫了，探头探脑的，看着厨房灶台上熬着的玉米排骨汤，非常心动。

但他现在肯定不能吃……

鸟自己在家也有些无聊，又吃了一小块苹果，想了想，飞到了二楼去。

白粼粼熟门熟路地站在门把手上，带着自己的身体“墩了墩”，很轻松就打开了。

随后的流程就比较紧张刺激了。

白粼粼先是叨开开机键，然后认真站在电脑屏幕前等待开机，随后正儿八经地输入密码。

开始战斗！

键盘其实是有些大的，鸟腿几乎要分叉，时不时还对用喙来叨一口。

最后打出来0-12-0的战绩。

“……”

白粼粼当然不服输，他好说歹说也是个学计算机出身的，电脑按键的问题而已，大约捯饬了有半个小时。

又美美开了一局。

不过这次自己不是人机操作了，队友却变人机了，技能乱放，上去送死，完了最后开麦一直说：

[欸，这里有活人吗？]

白粼粼怒了，翅膀一挥，开启麦克风。

[啾啾啾啾啾啾啾啾啾！！]

[啾啾啾啾！]

队友懵了，一直在左下角聊天框里问：

[哪里来的鸟？]

[不是哥们，用鸟骂人？]

[你可玩的太脏了。]

白粼粼生气了，在死了的时候，一个字一个敲：

[我家鸟来打，都比你玩的好。]

对面彻底破防了。

最后打完这局游戏已经中午了，二楼走廊里传来阿姨的声音。

“小鸟在哪里呀？”

白粼粼只好关了游戏，利索地踩了关机键，然后愤愤不平地用喙推了推鼠标。

人机！

简直是人机！

不过能打游戏还是幸福的，他扑棱翅膀飞到了门口，果然看见了阿姨，不过对方似乎没有要进来的意思，只是在等着。

妇人很是温和地道：“哎呀，我就猜你在里面呀，我给小鸟勾了个围兜。”

“来来来。”
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 6**

After coming through the door, the auntie placed the fresh vegetables she had bought onto the table, planning to make a few sandwiches while preheating the oven.

Waves of rich aroma soon began wafting from the kitchen.

Right at that moment, however, the phone in her pocket vibrated. The person on the other end sounded like a middle-aged man.

"Yes, Sir, I understand."

"Little Song only went to see his mother last time. He hasn't gone back recently."

"Alright, yes, I understand."

Perched atop the antique chandelier, Bai Linlin let his avian head droop down, observing this new "human" with utmost seriousness.

The auntie let out a sigh after hanging up, but she quickly got back to work with brisk efficiency. Yet when she opened the refrigerator, she froze for a moment.

The inside was a complete mess, with vegetables and carrots bearing tiny, pitted peck marks.

Bai Linlin stretched his bird legs. A speck of yogurt lingered on his stubby beak, but he smacked it clean in no time.

*Resuming observation.*

Before the auntie could take her next step, her phone rang again. This time, it was Song Yu.

"Auntie Zhang, I sent you a message earlier. You don't need to come over to cook for me."

The voice from the receiver was quite cold, yet maintained a polite and courteous distance.

Catching herself in a bind, Auntie Zhang could only explain awkwardly, "I... I saw it, but... it's hard to explain to your father."

The smart lock of the villa had master access keys; even though Song Yu's father was abroad, he could still manage authorization remotely.

There was a silence on the other end.

Song Yu sounded almost irritable. "Then I'm coming back."

Bai Linlin could only gather a rough idea of what was happening. Perched on the chandelier, he had to tilt his head lower to listen closely.

It was mostly Auntie Zhang apologizing repeatedly, saying she would leave as soon as she finished cooking, while also trying to persuade him:

"Little Song, focus on your classes. It's my fault... My family is really tight on money right now, so I can't afford to lose this job. If you take leave, the school will definitely contact your father, so please don't..."

Listening to this made Bai Linlin feel suffocated.

*What a messy situation.*

He couldn't catch what was said next, but the auntie's tone changed abruptly, and she began looking around anxiously.

"Is that so? Oh dear, I haven't seen it!"

Feeling even more guilty, the woman paced back and forth in the kitchen, even preparing to search the living room.

Bai Linlin had been staring down. Trying to track her movement required straining his neck, so he shifted his claws slightly—but the antique chandelier clattered noisily at the slightest movement.

The moment he shifted, the auntie froze and looked straight up.

"Little Song, I found it."

Ten minutes later—

On Song Yu's phone screen, a plump, round bird head appeared. Standing on the dining table, its stubby beak opened and closed slightly, seemingly letting out a yawn.

It had taken Auntie Zhang quite an effort to coax him down. She tried bird food first, which failed completely, before finally resorting to the sliced cooked ham she had brought over.

Yet before Bai Linlin could snag a single bite, a massive phone camera was pointed right at him.

The auntie enthusiastically framed the little bird in the shot, showering him with genuine praise:

"Oh my, look at you! So handsome, so pretty!"

"Little bird, look at the camera!"

"Your master is watching you!"

Bai Linlin felt his bird face flush with embarrassment for a moment. *Why is she talking to me like a toddler?*

The auntie even flipped the camera, using her hands as a makeshift stand so the bird could see his owner on the screen.

Song Yu leaned against a railing. There was no one around him; he seemed to be on a rooftop. His bangs blew gently in the breeze, and his features looked exceptionally striking in the sunlight.

"..."

Bai Linlin didn't know what to say. After pondering for a moment, he let out a few chirps toward the screen.

Phone cameras distort close-up images, making his round bird head take up the entire screen. As his short beak opened and closed, it looked almost as if he were nuzzling right up against the boy's face.

Song Yu remained expressionless—and took a screenshot.

Auntie Zhang carried most of the conversation during the video call.

"Have you named it yet, Little Song?"

"Not yet."

"Well, you definitely should. A pet is part of the family, too. Oh my, how wonderful."

The auntie was genuinely relieved. Having taken care of the boy for half a year, she knew a bit about the Song family's affairs. Understanding his situation made it impossible not to feel heartbroken for him.

A little bird was good. A little bird could keep Little Song company.

Bai Linlin stood prim and proper on the dining table. He found it a bit boring at first, but as he stared at Song Yu on the screen, for reasons unknown, he pecked at it.

"..."

The youth looked down, his gaze serene.

Bai Linlin tilted his bird head and took another peck.

"..."

In the end, the ringing of the class bell put an end to this "boring" interaction. As Auntie Zhang picked up her phone to say a few final words, the bird waddled forward, craning his head curiously.

"What would you like for lunch, Little Song? I'll prepare it in advance."

"Alright, alright. Don't worry, I haven't opened any doors or windows. The little bird is completely safe."

...

Bai Linlin spotted his moment, fluttered his wings, flew over, and pecked the phone screen.

He hit the end-call button square in the center.

The auntie gasped in amazement once more, showering the bird with compliments so endlessly that she even forgot about cooking for a moment.

Bai Linlin reservedly showed off another talent, flying a graceful lap above the table before landing perfectly.

"Little bird, you fly so well!"

"Come, come, let me take some pictures of you and send them to our Little Song."

Bai Linlin's vanity swelled tremendously. *Who knew life could be so wonderful after giving up being human?*

–

About thirty minutes later.

After carefully checking her phone, Auntie Zhang cut a fingernail-sized piece of apple for the bird, sending all the photos she had just taken over to Song Yu.

She never worried about the boy's studies. Even though he was ill, he seemed to rank first every single year.

Relaxing a bit was good for him.

Bai Linlin snatched the apple piece and devoured it eagerly. Craning his neck, he eyed the corn and pork rib soup simmering on the kitchen stove, deeply tempted.

Though he definitely couldn't eat that right now...

Feeling a bit bored at home alone, he ate another tiny scrap of apple, pondered for a moment, and flew up to the second floor.

Familiar with the route, Bai Linlin landed on the doorknob, bouncing his body up and down a couple of times to turn it open effortlessly.

What followed was a thrilling, edge-of-your-seat process.

First, Bai Linlin pecked the power button, stood seriously in front of the monitor waiting for it to boot up, and methodically pecked in the password.

Time to battle!

The keyboard was actually quite large for him. His bird legs were stretched nearly into a split, and he occasionally had to use his beak to tap a key.

In the end, he scored a stunning KDA of 0-12-0.

"..."

Naturally, Bai Linlin refused to accept defeat. He was a computer science major, after all! It was just a minor issue with keyboard adaptation. After fiddling around for about half an hour, he joyfully started another match.

However, while he was no longer playing like an AI bot this time, his teammate turned into one—spamming skills randomly, feeding the enemy, and finally turning on the mic to keep asking:

[Hey, any living human here?]

Bai Linlin flew into a rage. With a flick of his wing, he unmuted the mic.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!!"

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

His teammate was bewildered, constantly typing in the bottom-left chat box:

[Where did a bird come from?]

[Bro, you using a bird to flame people?]

[That's playing dirty.]

Bai Linlin was furious. While waiting to respawn, he typed out letter by letter:

[Even my bird plays better than you.]

The teammate's mental state completely collapsed.

By the time the match finished, it was already noon. Auntie Zhang's voice echoed from the second-floor hallway.

"Where is the little bird?"

Bai Linlin had no choice but to exit the game, nimbly stepping on the shutdown key before indignantly pushing the mouse with his beak.

*Bots! Total bots!*

Still, being able to play video games was pure bliss. Fluttering his wings, he flew over to the doorway and indeed saw Auntie Zhang. However, she didn't seem inclined to come inside, merely waiting at the door.

The woman said gently, "My, I guessed you'd be in here! I crocheted a little bib for you."

"Come, come."

chunks.chineseText:
宋郁中午回来的时候，看到的就是带着黄色围兜的小鸟，在餐桌那里使劲地撬保温罩。

他抬手替鸟掀开了。

白粼粼不由得脑袋探了过去，但被一把握住了，拿开。

少年拉开椅子坐下，看到了桌上的便条：

——阿姨晚上再过来做饭，小宋你放心，我不会和你爸爸说你养小鸟这件事的。

——要开开心心的。

宋郁抬手收了起来，照旧和往常一样，吃完饭，收拾自己的碗筷，上楼，休息。

身后一路跟着只“小鸡”。

白粼粼更多的其实还是好奇，因为宋郁一看就是少爷，怎么手腕上有划痕……

鸟很担忧。

他还是不由自主开始跟随行为。

人去卧室，小鸟飞到人肩头上搭乘“便车”。

人去书桌，小鸟叼着草稿纸啃啃啃。

人去洗手间，小鸟大摇大摆地也要跟着去……

砰！

门被关上了，鸟爪在地板上滑了下。

白粼粼：“……”

切，不去就不去。

他又飞到了书桌上，兢兢业业地又啃那个封皮，或许是做了鸟了，没有任何烦恼，白粼粼比较热衷于给自己尾羽上插纸条。

好玩。

他没一会就啃得差不多了。

宋郁从洗手间出来的时候，垂眸看着那本没有封皮的教辅书，沉默了一会。

总之是相安无事了几天。

人上学，鸟在家自由活动。

都很平静。

但变故发生在周末的那天。

是个阴天，外面在下雨，白粼粼本来是窝在书桌上的笔筒的，毛绒绒的像个挂件。

鸟眼也是闭着的。

主要是因为不分昼夜偷偷打游戏的，他困得要死。

宋郁的号根本就是消遣用的，他从来不看历史战绩，也不在意分段，而这恰恰给了鸟可乘之机。

但还是有点麻烦的，因为键位离的远，鸟腿要劈叉，打完一局酸酸的。

翅根也酸酸的。

宋郁本来是在看书，垂眸看了眼手机屏幕，不知道是看到什么了，扯了扯唇，面色有些冷。

然后起身出门了。

抽走了笔筒的工笔刀。

鸟本来也要去，都歪歪扭扭站在“人”的肩膀了，但还是被一把握住拿下来了，又给放到了笔筒里。

困乏极了，鸟又打了个哈欠。

朦胧之中，白粼粼似乎感觉有手指在自己的喙上戳了下，耳边有微凉的声音：

“我出门一趟。”

后面的事情不太清晰了，只是记得宋郁回来的时候很晚了，浑身湿透，皮肤冷白，指尖有血顺着往下滴。

当时阿姨正好在准备晚饭，吓得不轻，着急去拿绷带处理了。

白粼粼站在桌上，来回走了几圈，最后飞到了少年的肩头。

但还没来得及啾啾。

“我身上湿，待会再上来好不好？”

宋郁侧眸看了过去，语调温和，神色看着很是平静，丝毫不像是刚刚在外面自残过。

白粼粼判断了下，觉得他可能是见了什么人。

但还没来得及仔细思考，鸟被身后的人拿了下来。

阿姨面色很是担忧，一边抽空用手指摸了摸小鸟脑袋，一边拿出来绷带给宋郁缠手上的伤口。

其实动作很熟练。

少年本来是垂眸看着伤口的，但是后面突兀地转头，看着鸟。

白粼粼：“……”

孩子，你这很严重好不好？

看我干什么？

白粼粼尽管不太了解现在的青春期小朋友，但他还是梳理了下翅膀，慢吞吞地往桌边挪动，鸟腿一点点地伸了过去。

羽毛蓬松。

贴了过来。

宋郁受伤的是左手，右手在桌面上放着，他正在低头看着鸟。

流血了。

它不害怕么？

白粼粼仰头看了过去，也就在对视的时候，宋郁语气没有任何起伏地道：

“张姨。”

“我妈妈二胎出生了。”
chunks.englishText:
When Song Yu returned at noon, what greeted his eyes was a little bird wearing a yellow bib, desperately trying to pry open the insulated food cover on the dining table.

He reached out and lifted it for the bird.

Bai Linlin instinctively poked his head forward, only to be caught in a gentle grasp and set aside.

The youth pulled out a chair and sat down, noticing a sticky note left on the table:

—*I’ll be back this evening to make dinner. Don't worry, Xiao Song, I won’t tell your father about the little bird.*

—*Remember to be happy.*

Song Yu lifted his hand to put the note away. Just as usual, he finished his lunch, cleared his own dishes, and headed upstairs to rest.

All the while, a little "chick" trailed close behind him.

Truth be told, Bai Linlin was mostly driven by curiosity. Song Yu was clearly a young master born into privilege, so why were there slash marks on his wrist...?

The bird was quite worried.

Involuntarily, he began to shadow the boy’s every move.

When the human went to the bedroom, the little bird flew onto his shoulder to catch a free ride.

When the human went to the desk, the little bird nibbled away diligently on scrap paper.

When the human went to the bathroom, the little bird swaggered right along, fully intending to follow inside...

*Bang!*

The door shut tight, and the little bird’s talons slipped on the slick floorboards.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Hmph. Fine, see if I care.*

He fluttered back over to the desk and devotedly resumed gnawing on the book cover. Perhaps because he was a bird now and free from worldly troubles, Bai Linlin had developed a keen interest in tucking strips of paper into his tail feathers.

It was fun.

In no time at all, he had chewed through most of it.

When Song Yu emerged from the bathroom, his gaze drifted down to the coverless study workbook. He fell silent for a long moment.

All in all, the next few days passed in peaceful coexistence.

The human went to school, while the bird enjoyed free rein at home.

Everything remained calm.

The disruption, however, arrived on the weekend.

It was an overcast day, drizzling outside. Bai Linlin had originally curled up inside the pen holder on the desk, looking like a fluffy, feathery trinket.

His beady eyes were shut.

Mainly because he had been secretly playing video games day and night, leaving him dead tired.

Song Yu’s gaming account was purely for leisure; he never checked his match history, nor did he care about his competitive rank. This indifference provided the bird with the perfect opening.

Still, it was quite an ordeal. The keys were spaced so far apart that the bird had to do full splits, leaving his legs aching after every single match.

The base of his wings throbbed, too.

Song Yu had been reading, but he glanced down at his phone screen. Whatever flashed across it made his lips twist slightly, his expression chilling over.

He then rose to his feet, preparing to head out.

From the pen holder, he slipped out a craft knife.

The bird had intended to tag along, already wobbling precariously on the human's shoulder, but a hand enveloped him once more, lifting him off and placing him right back into the pen holder.

Exhaustion weighed heavily on him, and the bird let out another yawn.

In a daze, Bai Linlin seemed to feel a finger lightly tap against his beak, accompanied by a cool, faint voice:

"I'm stepping out for a bit."

The events after that were rather hazy. All he remembered was that Song Yu returned very late, completely soaked through. His skin was a deathly, cold white, and blood dripped steadily from his fingertips.

Auntie happened to be preparing dinner at the time and was frightened out of her wits, frantically rushing to grab bandages to tend to his injuries.

Bai Linlin stood on the table, pacing back and forth for a few turns before fluttering onto the youth's shoulder.

Yet before he could even let out a chirp—

"I'm wet all over. How about coming up later?"

Song Yu glanced sidelong at him, his tone gentle and his countenance remarkably serene—not in the least resembling someone who had just engaged in self-harm out in the rain.

Bai Linlin assessed the situation and surmised that he had probably gone to meet someone.

Before he could mull over it any further, a pair of hands lifted the bird away from behind.

Worry etched deep into her face, Auntie stole a brief moment to stroke the little bird’s head with a finger before pulling out the bandages to wrap Song Yu's wounded hand.

Her movements, in fact, were remarkably practiced.

The youth had initially been staring down at his wounds, but then he abruptly turned his head, fixing his gaze on the bird.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Kid, this is serious, all right?*

*What are you staring at me for?*

Though Bai Linlin did not understand much about today’s moody teenagers, he still preened his wings, shuffled slowly toward the edge of the table, and cautiously stretched his little legs forward.

Feathers puffed up.

He snuggled closer.

Song Yu’s left hand was the one injured; his right hand rested flat upon the table as he looked down at the little bird.

There was blood.

Was it not afraid?

Bai Linlin tilted his head up to look at him. And just as their gazes met, Song Yu spoke in a tone entirely devoid of emotion:

"Auntie Zhang."

"My mother's second child has been born."

chunks.chineseText:
第7章

别墅外头还在下雨。

宋郁在椅子上坐着，身上单薄，垂眸看着鸟，静静地道：

“她都三十九了。”

白粼粼鸟眼都瞪大了点，这不是高龄产妇么？

但阿姨闻言也只是怔了下，张了张嘴，也不知道说什么，最后选择岔开话题了：

“外头这么凉，快去冲个热水澡。”

“要注意别碰手啊。”

宋郁面色冷白，不知道在想什么，似乎是觉得没意思，过了一会起身去楼上了。

鸟本来也打算跟上去的，但是被阿姨给留下来擦鸟爪了。

白粼粼残留点人的生活习惯，索性直接坐在桌子上了，爪子被捏住了。

阿姨愁容满面的，叹了口气，自言自语道：

“都离婚十多年了，要是不管就彻底别联系……”

“非让孩子过去做什么。”

“这不是剜人的心么。”

白粼粼其实还是有些意外的，“离婚”他其实可以猜到，毕竟这个房子好像只有宋郁一个人住。

但是，离婚十多年了？

那二胎……

宋郁这个说法，有把自己算在内吗？

鸟心里有个隐隐的猜想，不自觉地仰头往楼上看，然后扑棱翅膀飞过去了。

与此同时，国外。

陈开鹤是在S州的私立医院里得知宋郁母亲又生了一个孩子的消息的，那张打了码的合照都传到文娱榜头条了。

老头儿面色很是铁青，当即就和宋郁的姥爷打了越洋电话。

“江连成，你怎么教你女儿的，她是不是有病！”

江连成是南市有名的书画家，也是宋郁母亲江芮的父亲，最近刚上任美术协会的副主席，正是春风得意的时候。

现下被这么一阵吼，他好半天没反应过来，过了一会才迟疑地问：

“你说芮芮？”

江芮早年同宋父离婚后，消沉了几年，而后看上一个娱乐圈的制片人。

这本无可厚非。

但问题是那男人爱营销家庭美满人设，每次都会让江芮在聚会上带上她与前夫的儿子，不经意让媒体拍摄些照片，造舆论，借机宣传自己的影视剧。

很令人作呕的行为。

第一次是在宋郁读小学的时候，那时孩子很小，正是思念妈妈的时候，江芮很轻而易举就把人接走了。

隔天照片就爆出来了，是在一个包厢里，小小的孩子坐在一旁，旁边是自己微微显怀的母亲和陌生的男人。

宋郁回到家就被父亲扇了一巴掌，指责他是吃里爬外的东西。

可这对于一个想要妈妈的孩子来说，是无妄之灾。

宋郁也是在那时才知道，那些“离婚了我也是你爸爸妈妈”的话，通通都是骗人的。

经年累月，一朝一岁。

江芮再婚都是很久远的事了，算上今年的这一胎，刚好为那制片人添了一对儿女了。

但不知道她是后知后觉自己还有个儿子，还是单纯想要讨好现任丈夫，在前几天的满月酒上又邀请了宋郁。

阖家团圆，留影纪念。

陈开鹤当时看到头条的照片就恼火得不行，整篇文章几乎都在写那制片人的作品，还明里暗里写了“华秉产业”的股份动荡一事，完全是故意的。

现在宋家这个局势，华秉真去发律师函，是把江芮这个生母放在什么位置？

不告。

那其实就是放任“伤害”。

江芮不可能不知道宋郁生病了，或者说，她从头到尾都觉得那是在博关注。

不然不会时隔多年，让媒体再发第二次合影。

“不然呢！老宋是植物人了，不是死了。”

陈开鹤听到对面那不确定的语气就恼火，装什么不知道，又道：

“他就这么一个孙子！”

宋郁的爷爷是宋峥国，早年从军，中年从商，一手创办了华秉实业，是实打实的白手起家。

但也正是因为经历的坎坷，导致他尤为看不惯三心二意的人，自从儿子儿媳离婚后，就始终不同意儿子再婚。

理由是宋郁还太小。

即使后面闹出来私生子丑闻，宋峥国也依然铁血不认，甚至架空了儿子在华秉的权力，大有要修改遗产分配书的意思。

但就在这个紧要关头，宋峥国却在家中心脑血管疾病复发，救治不及时，成了植物人，至今仍在S州疗养。

“师兄，你别急……”

江连成此刻在书房，面色也是有点难看，只能先出声安抚道。

没办法，陈开鹤对他有知遇之恩，当年自己岌岌无名的时候，是靠着对方一路引荐，他才能有现在的名气。

也才……高攀上宋家。

尽管现在是“三十年河西”了，但还是要面上过得去，不能给落人话柄，他斟酌了下，试着说道：

“我回头，不，我现在就去给江芮打电话，让她好好反省反省！”

陈开鹤一听这话就知道是敷衍，尽管气得没办法，但也没失了理智，闭了闭眼把电话给撂了。

这都什么人……

真是可怜了老宋。

生出来的儿子巴不得自己永远植物人；疼爱的孙子被他父亲困在南市、连来探望也做不到。

宋家简直是反了天了。

陈开鹤愈发不后悔自己独身主义的选择，要是他晚年面临峥国这样子的烂摊子。

他就不是植物人了。

他直接死。

-

锦园。

白粼粼其实还是没太理清楚宋家的人物关系，因为他目前见到的宋家人……只有宋郁一个。

其余一概不知。

但自从那天淋雨之后，他就发现少年更加沉默寡言了，有好几次都忘记给他添粮了。

宋郁可能也注意到了自己的反常，于是同阿姨说了帮忙照看小鸟的事，还给转了几千块，但阿姨没要。

白粼粼其实觉得自己根本不需要照顾，因为他最近过得很是滋润。

托宋郁的福，他这几天吃了鸡蛋卷饼、牛肉酥、青椒炒饭、杨枝甘露、鲜鱼丸、糖醋排骨……

一套流程是这样的，鸟在玄关目送阿姨离开，飞到桌子上，身躯下压，用短短的喙开始撬保温罩，钻进去。

而后开启美食之旅。

白粼粼简直叨得不知天地为何物，但他还是有分寸的，偷吃完会小心翼翼把饭菜恢复原状。

具体表现为：

把三块排骨凑成一盘菜。

不过宋郁压根没有发现，或者说是根本没有精力在意，他很明显地消沉了下来。

是抑郁期。

他的注意力持续下降。

一天晚上，别墅里很是安静。

宋郁在餐厅吃饭。

“啾啾？”

鸟飞了过来，板板正正地站在“人”的筷子上……

开始往下滑溜。

白粼粼最后爪子歪歪扭扭的，勉强卡在宋郁的虎口上。

“你是不是变重了点？”

宋郁身着黑色毛衣，高领修身，垂眸看着手背上的小鸟，眼皮掀开了点，轻声道。

白粼粼：“……”

你再说，再说我就下来了啊。

宋郁看了很久，而后用手指碰了碰小鸟胸前的羽毛，力道不轻不重，白粼粼一开始还扭了扭身子，之后就彻底不动了。

因为还挺舒服的。

鸟眯了眯眼，非常满意。

但就在这时。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 7

Rain was still pouring outside the villa.

Song Yu sat in a chair, dressed in thin layers, lowering his gaze toward the bird as he said quietly,

"She is already thirty-nine."

The bird Bailinlin’s eyes widened slightly. Wasn't that an advanced-maternal-age pregnancy?

Yet the housekeeper only paused at these words, her mouth opening slightly. Unsure of what to say, she ultimately chose to change the subject.

"It's so chilly outside. Go take a hot shower quickly."

"And remember not to get your hands wet."

Song Yu’s face was pale and cold, his thoughts unreadable. Seeming to find no point in lingering, he stood up a moment later and headed upstairs.

The bird had originally intended to follow him, but was intercepted by the housekeeper to have its claws wiped down.

Bailinlin still retained some human habits, so he simply sat right on the table while his claws were gently held in place.

With a worried frown, the housekeeper let out a sigh and muttered to herself,

"They've been divorced for over ten years. If you're going to wash your hands of it, cut ties completely..."

"Why on earth drag the child into this?"

"Isn't this just carving out a piece of someone's heart?"

Bailinlin was actually quite surprised. He could guess the part about the "divorce," considering this house seemed to be inhabited solely by Song Yu.

However... divorced for over ten years?

Then what about this second child...

In making that remark, had Song Yu included himself in the count?

A faint speculation took root in the bird's mind. Without thinking, he raised his head to look upstairs, then fluttered his wings and flew up.

Meanwhile, overseas.

Chen Kehe learned the news of Song Yu’s mother giving birth to yet another child while at a private hospital in State S. That mosaic-censored family photo had already made the headlines of the entertainment trending lists.

The old man’s face turned livid. He immediately placed a transoceanic call to Song Yu’s maternal grandfather.

"Jiang Liancheng, how the hell did you raise your daughter? Has she lost her mind?!"

Jiang Liancheng was a renowned calligrapher and painter in Nanshi, as well as the father of Song Yu’s mother, Jiang Rui. Having recently assumed office as the vice chairman of the Fine Arts Association, he was currently riding the crest of success.

Blindsided by this sudden bellow, it took him quite a while to react. After a moment, he asked tentatively,

"Are you talking about Ruirui?"

After divorcing Song Yu’s father in her early years, Jiang Rui had spent a few years feeling low before taking a fancy to a producer in the entertainment circle.

In itself, that was nothing out of the ordinary.

The problem, however, was that the man loved to market an image of domestic bliss, routinely having Jiang Rui bring her ex-husband's son along to gatherings. He would subtly have the media snap a few photos, stirring up public opinion as a way to promote his own film and television projects.

It was a thoroughly nauseating practice.

The first time it happened was when Song Yu was still in primary school. The child was very young back then, at an age when he deeply missed his mother, and Jiang Rui had easily coaxed him into going with her.

The photos exploded across the internet the very next day. They showed the tiny child sitting quietly off to the side, flanked by his mother—whose belly was slightly swelling with pregnancy—and a strange man.

Upon returning home, Song Yu was met with a slap across the face from his father, who rebuked him as a traitor who ate inside and out.

Yet for a child who simply longed for his mother, this was an unmitigated disaster.

It was also at that moment that Song Yu learned those words—"Even if we're divorced, I'll still be your mom and dad"—were absolute lies.

As the years accumulated, year by year.

Jiang Rui’s remarriage was a matter of the distant past. Counting this current litter, she had given the producer a son and a daughter.

Whether she had belatedly realized she still had another son, or simply wanted to curry favor with her current husband, she had once again invited Song Yu to the full-month banquet held a few days prior.

A joyful family reunion, captured on film as a commemorative keepsake.

Upon seeing the headline photo at the time, Chen Kehe had been utterly enraged. Nearly the entire article was dedicated to praising the producer's works, while also making overt and covert references to the stock fluctuations of "Hua Bing Enterprises"—it was entirely deliberate.

With the current situation in the Song family, if Hua Bing were to actually issue a legal notice, where would that leave Jiang Rui, his biological mother?

Not suing.

That was essentially condoning the "harm."

It was impossible that Jiang Rui didn't know Song Yu was sick; or rather, from beginning to end, she likely believed he was simply vying for attention.

Otherwise, after all these years, she wouldn't have let the media publish a second joint photograph.

"What else could I mean?! Old Song is in a vegetative state, he isn't dead!"

Hearing that uncertain tone from the other end only fueled Chen Kehe’s fury. What was the man pretending not to know for? He pressed on,

"He only has this one grandson!"

Song Yu’s grandfather was Song Zhengguo, who had served in the military in his early years before turning to commerce in middle age. Single-handedly founding Hua Bing Industries, he was a true self-made man.

Yet it was precisely because of these rugged trials that he held a particular contempt for fickle people. Ever since his son and daughter-in-law divorced, he had consistently refused to allow his son to remarry.

His stated reason was that Song Yu was still too young.

Even when the illegitimate child scandal erupted later on, Song Zhengguo maintained his iron-fisted refusal to acknowledge them. He even stripped his son of his power within Hua Bing, strongly hinting at an intention to revise the will regarding the distribution of his estate.

Yet right at this critical juncture, Song Zhengguo suffered a recurrence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease at home. Failing to receive timely medical rescue, he slipped into a vegetative state and was still convalescing in State S to this day.

"Senior Brother, don't be anxious..."

In his study at that moment, Jiang Liancheng wore an equally unsightly expression as he hurriedly offered words of pacification.

There was no helping it; Chen Kehe was his benefactor who had recognized his talent. Back when he was entirely obscure, it was thanks to the other man’s repeated recommendations that he had attained his present renown.

And had managed to... climb high into the Song family.

Though the tables had turned now and "thirty years of river flows east, thirty years west," he still had to maintain appearances to avoid giving others grounds for gossip. Pondering for a moment, he tested the waters by saying,

"I'll turn around—no, I'll call Jiang Rui right now and tell her to reflect properly on herself!"

Hearing this, Chen Kehe knew at once it was just perfunctory nonsense. Though burning with helplessness, he hadn't lost his reason; closing his eyes, he slammed the phone down.

What kind of people were these...

It was simply a pity for Old Song.

The son he had spawned wished nothing more than for him to remain a vegetable forever; the grandson he cherished was trapped in Nanshi by his father, unable even to pay a visit.

The Song family had truly turned upside down.

Chen Kehe grew increasingly glad of his choice to remain a celibate bachelor. If he were to face a mess like Zhengguo's in his old age,

he wouldn't become a vegetable.

He'd just drop dead.

-

Jin Yuan.

Bailinlin still hadn't quite sorted out the relationships within the Song family, because the only member of the Song family he had laid eyes on thus far... was Song Yu himself.

As for the rest, he knew nothing.

However, ever since getting caught in the rain that day, he noticed that the young man had become even more taciturn, on several occasions forgetting to refill his food bowl.

Song Yu likely noticed his own abnormality as well, and had instructed the housekeeper to help look after the little bird, even trying to transfer a few thousand yuan, which the housekeeper had refused.

Bailinlin felt he didn't need looking after at all, as his recent days had been remarkably plush.

Thanks to Song Yu’s blessing, over the past few days he had feasted on egg crepe rolls, beef pastries, green pepper fried rice, mango sago pomelo, fresh fish balls, sweet and sour pork ribs...

The standard routine went like this: the bird would watch the housekeeper leave from the entryway, flutter onto the table, flatten his body, and use his short beak to pry open the insulation cover before tunneling inside.

Thus began his culinary journey.

Bailinlin would peck away in blissful oblivion, yet he maintained a sense of propriety—after secretly gorging himself, he would meticulously restore the dishes to their original appearance.

Specifically:

Piecing three spare ribs back together to look like a complete dish.

Yet Song Yu didn't notice this in the slightest—or rather, he lacked the energy to care. He was sinking into a state of profound depression.

It was his depressive phase.

His attention span continued to plummet.

One evening, the villa was dead quiet.

Song Yu was eating dinner in the dining room.

"Chirp?"

The bird flew over, perching stiffly and formally right on the "human's" chopsticks...

And immediately began sliding downward.

In the end, Bailinlin's claws ended up crookedly wedged against the crook of Song Yu’s thumb.

"Did you get a little heavier?"

Wearing a black, high-collared, form-fitting sweater, Song Yu lowered his gaze to look at the little bird on the back of his hand. Lifting his eyelids slightly, he said softly,

Bailinlin: "..."

Say that again, and I'll fly right down.

Song Yu stared for a long time, then used his finger to gently stroke the feathers on the little bird's chest, applying just the right amount of pressure. Initially, Bailinlin squirmed a little, but soon went completely still.

Because it actually felt quite nice.

The bird narrowed his eyes in supreme satisfaction.

Yet right at that moment—

chunks.chineseText:
少年蹙眉喃喃道：“是刀胸吗？”

白粼粼愣了下，这是什么东西？

宋郁查过鹦鹉的饲养知识，刀胸是一种疾病，多发于营养不良的小鸟，说是胸部位置像是一把刀。

白粼粼被拿了下来，然后感觉是被拍了照，宋郁修长的手指在手机屏幕上滑动。

鸟好奇，探头去看。

发现是“人”发了个帖子：

【这是刀胸了么？】

宋郁的确不想一直麻烦齐思扬，对方还有学业在身，他索性想着在网上问一问。

不过在等评论的时候，小鸟已经站在了他的袖子上，脑袋圆圆的，往下认真地看。

宋郁几乎走了下神。

帖子此刻有了几条评论：

【咦惹，这么肥美。】

下面紧跟着回复：

【小鸡别看是恶评。】

但白粼粼已经看到了，爪子都踩得用力了点，仰头就一顿抗议：

“啾啾啾啾！”

“啾啾啾！”

[胡说八道！]

[鸟不胖！]

宋郁其实难免有些错觉，它是……看得懂么？

修长的手指又滑动了下，但就在这时，鸟腿一伸，卡住了。

白粼粼又在低头看评论。

【呃呃，瘦得凸起是刀胸，胖得凹陷是肥缝。】

“啾啾啾啾！”

“啾啾啾啾啾！”

宋郁也听不懂，但能判断出他的小鸟不太乐意看到这些评论，于是把手机关了。

白粼粼很是不高兴，弯腰还叨了下已经黑掉的屏幕，但用力过猛，一脑袋栽进“人”的手掌心。

可那上面还缠着绷带。

白粼粼一下子老实了，他害怕碰到对方的伤口。

爪子都收了收。

但好在宋郁没有什么反应，只是把鸟放到了桌上，垂眸自己看那个帖子。

直到确定是一场乌龙之后，少年才把手机放到了一旁，开始吃已经冷掉的饭菜。

白粼粼歪了歪头，还是没看出来宋郁是个什么心情，只知道大概还是不好。

因为吃的药变多了。

-

大约半个月后，白粼粼意外地发现自己好像学会说话了，这是阿姨不断训练的结果，第一句就是：

“举头望明月。”

很有文化的一只小鸟。

阿姨连连鼓掌，给鸟捧场，还投喂了旺仔小馒头，一个劲地表扬：

“好棒好棒。”

“小宋知道一定很高兴。”

白粼粼鸟脸一红，羽毛蓬松，不好意思再说了。

不过还要旺仔小馒头。

鸟想要，鸟得到。

……

但宋郁的心情似乎仍然没有变好，一连回来几次都只是上楼打游戏，白粼粼一直陪着。

飞到少年肩头，伸着鸟腿，坐下。

直到有一天。

家里的阿姨突然被辞退了，这几乎是一个导火索，宋郁白天打了一通电话，那边好像是他的父亲，少年语气从头到尾都不好：

“这么爱管着我？那你自己怎么不亲自过来呢？”

“还是说，你守着我爷爷，是心里有鬼？”

宋郁身高已经一米八了，坐在岛台那里漫不经心地打电话，手里玩着一把工笔刀。

白粼粼一边偷偷听，一边左右摇摆地走过去，鸟头探了几下，快准狠地——

叼走了“危险玩具”。

宋郁其实是愣了下，连带着输出都停了。

电话那里的声音更加恼火，一连说了好几个“混账”和“无法无天”。

宋郁这才回了回神，抽空说了句：

“谢谢夸奖。”

电话那头的中年男人似乎是破防了，传出来些乱七八糟的杂音，还有一道关门的动静。

宋郁压根就没有在意，他左手的伤已经恢复完全，只是垂着眼皮，定定地看着前方：

桌前的小鸟叼着那把工笔刀，很是勤勤恳恳地往旁边走，或许是因为太沉了，啪嗒啪嗒走两步歇一步的。

最后停下来，鸟头转了转。

似乎是在环顾四周。

确定目标后，它又歪歪扭扭地往桌边走。

爪子并了并，尾羽上翘，开始蓄力。

宋郁就这么看着鸟用力一甩，把工笔刀扔进了垃圾桶里。

不过在鸟转身的时候，他不动声色地收回了目光，喉结微微滚了下。

手机里面仍然有聒噪的声音：

“宋郁！我告诉你，你一点都不如宋阳，亏你还是个哥哥。”

“你爷爷就算是醒了也会对你失望——”

宋郁面色直接变了，站了起来，冷声打断道：“你有什么资格提我爷爷！”

对面一下子安静了下来，好似是反应过来什么。

电话中断了。

白粼粼站在桌面上，安静如鸡。

宋郁情绪确实不好，垂着的手指都生理性地颤了颤，但他深呼吸了下，而后看过去桌面，恢复成正常的语气：

“对不起。”

“我把你的朋友弄丢了。”

白粼粼其实是愣了下的，朋友？说的是阿姨吗？

可是，他是他的小鸟。

没有宋郁，阿姨是不会来做饭的。

白粼粼还是想不通，直到宋郁伸过来一根手指，鸟自然而然抬腿上去了。

脑袋圆圆的。

鸟歪了歪头。

“我总是陪不了你很长时间。”

白粼粼闻言一下子警觉了起来，什么情况，不取名字是这个原因？

宋郁本来还想多解释几句，但唇角突然被创了一下，鸟已经扑棱翅膀飞过来了。

有钝钝的冲击力。

“啾啾啾啾。”

“啾啾啾。”

宋郁抬手接住了小鸟，低头问：“你自己在家里不会孤单么？”

白粼粼：“……”

不孤单，有吃有喝，有wifi。

当然，如果“人”愿意为鸟买一部手机的话，那就更好了。

白粼粼想到这里，脑海又自动浮现一串密码：

[******]

太堕落了，怎么能记得这么牢固……

宋郁其实不知道鸟的心理活动，他只是觉得他的小鸟会有些孤单。

大约晚上八点钟的时候，有人送过来新的鸟笼。

这已经是第九个窝了。

内部有木头制的小架子，还有栖杆，用来打发时间的麦秸秆、谷物棒等等，几乎一应俱全。

宋郁附身蹲在地板上，侧眸看着肩头的小鸟，其实有些无措。

它始终不进笼子。

“还是不喜欢？”

白粼粼点了点头，羽毛丰盈，像个毛球。

宋郁唇角微微压直，最终还是回了卧室，鸟扑棱翅膀就飞了下来。

站在了纸巾盒里。

“……”

齐思扬同他说过和尚鹦鹉的常见睡姿是没有仰躺的，陈爷爷也发过来了一些专业养鸟文件。

他不知道怎么办。

但也就这么一会儿，宋郁再低头去看，鸟已经躺下了。

安寝。

纸巾盒四四方方的，里面有个两脚朝天的鸟。

“。”

不太吉利的样子。

……

阿姨是因为没有及时传消息而被辞退的，宋启明，也就是宋郁的父亲，即使远在国外，也始终监控着自己的儿子。

或许是因为得知宋郁再次参加他母亲的“家庭聚会”过于恼火，倒是给直接忘了责问“养鸟这一事。

相安无事了几天。
chunks.englishText:
The youth frowned and muttered, "Is it knife-breast?"

Bai Linlin froze for a moment. *What on earth is that?*

Song Yu had researched parrot care before. "Knife-breast" was a condition common in malnourished young birds, so named because their breastbone jutted out like a blade.

Bai Linlin was set down, then felt himself being photographed as Song Yu's slender fingers swiped across his phone screen.

Curious, the little bird poked his head over to look.

He discovered that the "human" had posted on a forum:

[Is this knife-breast?]

Song Yu really didn't want to keep bothering Qi Siyang, who had his own studies to focus on, so he figured he would just ask online.

While waiting for replies, however, the little bird had already hopped onto his sleeve, tilting his round little head to look down intently at the screen.

Song Yu nearly lost his train of thought.

A few comments had popped up on the post:

[Eww, look at this chubby thing.]

Right below it came a reply:

[Don't look, little birdie! It's a mean comment.]

But Bai Linlin had already read it. His tiny claws gripped tighter, and he threw his head back in furious protest:

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

"Chirp chirp chirp!"

[*Nonsense!*]

[*This bird is NOT fat!*]

Song Yu couldn't help a fleeting illusion: *Can it... actually read?*

His slender fingers swiped the screen again, but right then, a bird leg stretched out and stomped on it, freezing the page.

Bai Linlin was leaning down to read more comments.

[Uhh, if it sticks out from being skinny, it's knife-breast; if it dips in from being fat, it's a fat cleavage.]

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

Song Yu couldn't understand him either, but he could tell his little bird was displeased with the comments, so he switched off his phone.

Bai Linlin was thoroughly annoyed. He bent down and gave the darkened screen a peck, but he used too much force, causing his head to plunge right into the "human's" palm.

Except that palm was still wrapped in bandages.

Bai Linlin instantly froze, terrified of poking the boy's wound.

He even tucked his little claws in tightly.

Fortunately, Song Yu showed no sign of pain. He simply set the bird down on the desk, lowering his eyes to read the thread himself.

Once he confirmed it was all a false alarm, the youth set his phone aside and began eating his now-cold meal.

Bai Linlin tilted his head, still unable to gauge Song Yu's mood, though he figured it was probably still bad.

Because the medication he took had increased.

-

About half a month later, Bai Linlin unexpectedly discovered that he seemed to have learned how to speak. This was the result of the housekeeper's continuous training. His very first sentence was:

"Raising my head, I gaze at the bright moon."

A truly cultured little bird.

The auntie clapped enthusiastically in applause, feeding him Wang Zai milk biscuit treats while showering him with praise:

"So clever, so clever!"

"Little Song will be so happy when he finds out."

Bai Linlin's avian face flushed red. Fluffing his feathers bashfully, he felt too shy to say any more.

Though he still wanted another Wang Zai milk biscuit.

Bird wants, bird gets.

……

Yet Song Yu's mood didn't seem to improve at all. Several times when he came home, he would just go upstairs to play games, with Bai Linlin keeping him company the whole time.

He would fly onto the youth's shoulder, stretch out his bird legs, and sit down.

Until one day...

The housekeeper was suddenly dismissed. This proved to be the spark that ignited the powder keg. That day, Song Yu made a phone call—seemingly to his father—and his tone was bitter from start to finish:

"You love controlling me so much? Then why don't you come over here yourself?"

"Or is it that you're staying by Grandfather's side because you have a guilty conscience?"

Song Yu was already 1.8 meters tall. Sitting casually by the kitchen island while on the phone, he idly twirled an exacto knife in his hand.

While sneakily eavesdropping, Bai Linlin waddled over, swaying left and right. His head poked forward a few times, and then—swift, precise, and ruthless—

He snatched away the "dangerous toy."

Song Yu actually froze for a moment, his stream of verbal attacks coming to a sudden halt.

The voice on the other end grew even more infuriated, spewing out insults like "bastard" and "utterly lawless."

Only then did Song Yu snap back to reality, taking a moment to reply:

"Thanks for the compliment."

The middle-aged man on the phone seemed to suffer a total breakdown, accompanied by noisy clattering sounds and the slam of a door.

Song Yu didn't care in the slightest. The injury on his left hand had fully healed. He simply lowered his eyelids, staring fixedly ahead:

On the desk, the little bird carried the exacto knife in its beak, diligently waddling sideways. Perhaps because it was too heavy, the bird took two pitter-patter steps before pausing to catch its breath.

Finally, it stopped and turned its head.

It seemed to be looking around the room.

Once it identified its target, it wobbled toward the edge of the desk.

Bringing its claws together and sticking its tail feathers up in the air, it began to gear up.

Song Yu watched as the bird gave a hard fling, tossing the exacto knife right into the trash can.

However, the moment the bird turned back, he quietly withdrew his gaze, his Adam's apple bobbing slightly.

The noisy voice still blared from the phone:

"Song Yu! I'm telling you, you're not half the boy Song Yang is, and you call yourself an older brother?!"

"Even if your grandfather wakes up, he'll be thoroughly disappointed in you—"

Song Yu's expression instantly turned cold. Standing up, he interrupted harshly, "What right do you have to mention my grandfather?!"

The other side fell silent all at once, as if suddenly realizing something.

The call cut off.

Bai Linlin stood on the tabletop, silent as a mouse.

Song Yu's mood was indeed terrible; even his hanging fingers trembled involuntarily. But he took a deep breath, looked over at the desk, and restored his voice to a normal tone:

"I'm sorry."

"I lost your friend."

Bai Linlin was actually taken aback. *Friend? Is he talking about the auntie?*

*But I'm his bird.*

*Without Song Yu, the auntie wouldn't be here cooking meals anyway.*

Bai Linlin still couldn't figure it out, until Song Yu extended a finger, and the bird naturally stepped up onto it.

Head round and fluffy.

The bird tilted his head.

"I can never stay with you for very long."

Hearing this, Bai Linlin instantly snapped to attention. *What's going on? Is THAT why he hasn't named me?*

Song Yu originally wanted to explain further, but his lips were suddenly hit—the bird had flapped its wings and flown right into his face.

A blunt, soft impact.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp."

"Chirp chirp chirp."

Song Yu raised his hands to catch the little bird, looking down to ask, "Aren't you lonely staying home all by yourself?"

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Not lonely at all. I've got food, drink, and Wi-Fi.*

*Of course, if the "human" were willing to buy a phone for the bird, that would be even better.*

Thinking of this, a string of passcode numbers automatically popped into his head:

[******]

*How shameful... How could I remember it so clearly?*

Song Yu had no idea what was going on in the bird's head; he simply worried his little bird might feel lonely.

At around eight in the evening, someone delivered a new bird cage.

This was already the ninth home he had gotten.

Inside were tiny wooden stands, perches, wheat straws for passing time, seed sticks, and just about everything imaginable.

Song Yu bent down and squatted on the floor, glancing at the bird on his shoulder, feeling somewhat helpless.

It simply refused to enter the cage.

"Still don't like it?"

Bai Linlin nodded, his plump plumage making him look like a fluffy ball.

Song Yu pressed his lips into a straight line and ultimately returned to the bedroom. The bird flapped its wings and flew down,

Landing right inside the tissue box.

"..."

Qi Siyang had told him that monk parakeets didn't typically sleep flat on their backs, and Grandpa Chen had also sent over some professional bird-keeping documents.

He didn't know what to do.

Yet after just a moment, when Song Yu looked down again, the bird was already lying down.

Fast asleep.

Inside the square tissue box lay a bird with both legs pointing straight up at the ceiling.

"..."

Looking like an ominous sight.

……

The housekeeper had been fired for failing to pass on information in a timely manner. Song Qiming—Song Yu's father—kept a constant eye on his son even from abroad.

Perhaps because he was furious upon learning that Song Yu had attended his mother's "family gathering" again, he completely forgot to interrogate him about keeping a bird.

Things remained peaceful for a few days.

chunks.chineseText:
“其实鹦鹉算是杂食动物，它可能会好奇人吃的东西，卤肉……不是很久之前吃的吗？现在没事就行。”

陈开鹤正在S州的一所档案馆里给宋郁通话，精气神仍然很好，因为医院那里说峥国的身体素质仍然保持得很好，有清醒的可能性。

而锦园这里正是午夜。

宋郁晚上会失眠，他洗完澡，发梢都是潮的，眉眼轮廓在台灯下显得很是清晰。

电话那边还有絮絮叨叨的声音：

“科学喂养是正确的，但是小鸟也没有那么脆弱，南美的和尚鹦鹉也是会叨走人类丢下的食物的。”

“听小齐说你给它买了很多东西？取名字了吗？”

陈开鹤很是慈爱地询问了几句，宋郁生病之后就有些孤僻了，同幼年时期是完全不一样了。

他不可能不心疼。

“没有。”

夜已经很深了，宋郁垂眸看着纸巾盒里的小鸟，心里很平静。

取名字……

“好了，你那边很晚了，早点睡觉。”

“S州这里我看着的，你爷爷没事，不要担心。”

陈开鹤在那边又嘱咐了几句，电话这才挂断。

时间很快来到五月。

宋郁其实找过几次阿姨，给了不少钱，他起初是不喜欢对方总是同宋启明发消息，但后面看到医院里的孩子，什么话也说不出了。

一共给了二十万。

说是鸟的围兜钱。

阿姨眼泪在脸上都划成线了，最后只是握着宋郁的手，嘱咐着要好好生活。

少年割腕过。

宋郁回到了家中，心情不算太好，他没有请回鸟的“朋友”，毕竟他看到过鸟很开心的样子。

现在是假期，别墅里没有其他人，显得倒是空荡荡的。

宋郁走到餐桌那边，不由得蹙眉，因为碟子里的鸟粮还是分毫未动。

或者说，是拨了两下。

好看着已经“动”过了。

鸟在敷衍。

宋郁有些心烦意乱，他试着去好好养，可是总是和教程上的不一样，不知道该怎么做。

也就在这时，楼上有扑棱翅膀的声音，蓝色小鸟从他的卧室里飞出来了。

最后稳稳地降落在“人”的肩头。

白粼粼有些心虚，他刚刚打完一局游戏……

“啾啾。”

宋郁垂眸把鸟拿了下来，面色有些难看，因为小鸟的羽毛边缘有些异常，漂亮的蓝羽主轴那里有横向的黑灰色纹路。

压力纹。

有营养不良的成因，也有情感上的因素。

可是齐思扬已经带过他的师弟来体检，小鸟很健康。

那显而易见是后者。

白粼粼的鸟头被微微卡住，他抽了抽自己的短喙，开始去叨人，不过也没太用力，就是咬一咬。

怎么还不放开他？

宋郁情绪变得很不好，但即使这样，也没有对鸟表露什么情绪，只是碰了碰小鸟的脑袋。

“啾啾啾？”

白粼粼歪了歪鸟头。

大约一个小时后，有些搬运工来了锦园，零零散散地在往二楼的一个房间里搬东西。

宋郁在旁边付了钱，似乎在沟通什么。

鸟刚在厨房转了一圈，现在看着人来人往的，在地板上啪嗒啪嗒地走着，也不想飞。

犹如一个走地鸡。

“结清了结清了。”

“那我们就先走了……”

那群上门送货的人员又都走了，不过转头的时候还吓了一跳，因为鸟在地上，仰头看着他们，挡住路了。

宋郁面色温和，只是半蹲把手伸过去了，鸟很自然地抬了抬腿，站得稳稳当当。

起驾。

“不好意思，它不喜欢笼子，就在外面玩。”

工作人员点了点头，表示理解，不过走的时候还是感叹：

这年头，鸟都有独立房间了……

是的，宋郁直接让人过来安装了一套类似于攀爬架的木头装置，上面还有各种各样的小树屋，房间里的空调全程开着。

很豪华了。

但结果仍然不算太好，鸟只是在房间里飞了一圈，叼着一根麦秸秆回来了，站在宋郁肩头上。

圆滚滚的脑袋歪了歪。

又兢兢业业地把麦秸杆插在自己尾羽上了。

白粼粼的想法很简单，他又没有口袋，要么只能一路叼着，要么插身上去。

但他没想到的是——

“是发情了吗？”

宋郁原来也见过小鸟往自己尾羽里插纸条，当时他有查过，说是准备筑巢的行为。

但这多发于母鸟身上。

“啾啾啾啾！！啾啾啾！”

白粼粼整个鸟都红温了，说的什么话，说的什么话！

他直接一顿哐哐叫，而后很用力地叨了一口宋郁的手，飞到门外去了。

宋郁有些愣，手指流血了。

它好生气。

但他又觉得正常，可能发情期情绪不好……

可爱。

事情并没有那么容易过去，宋郁发现鸟在和他生气，一整个周末，没有靠近过来。

只是啪嗒啪嗒在地上走。

毛茸茸的。

宋郁不知道怎么办，他没有和小鸟沟通的经验。

尤其是好几天，它都不吃鸟粮的情况。

宋郁的确开始有些失控，他也没有怎么吃饭，而是很担心鸟会死掉。

情绪也很消沉。

但白粼粼其实根本就没有绝食的意思，他已经完全熟悉了这个别墅的构造，吃零食简直是熟门熟路的。

鸟圆嘟嘟的。

丝毫不瘦。

就是还是很生气！

宋郁一个小孩子，怎么能说那种话！

白粼粼虽然是鸟的身躯，但是他的内心仍然是个“成年人”，被那么一说……像被调戏了一样。

母胎单身需要缓好几天。

但他不知道的是，宋郁已经因为这件事吃了翻倍的药了，几乎出现了视力模糊的情况。

饲养宠物的确有助于心理调节。

但一旦死亡或者被宠物拒绝靠近，会起到极大的反作用。

白粼粼忘记自己没有吃鸟粮这件事了，但这在宋郁看来，是绝食。

此刻是中午，卧室门始终是开着的。

宋郁在房间里打游戏，面色冷白，电脑页面不断切换，挂脖耳机里传来一些击杀的通报。

他的心脏在很快地跳动，视野也变得模糊，头晕目眩。

养不好。

就是养不好。

宋郁起身仰躺在床上，手盖住了眼睛，视野里的黑色物质在翻涌、扭动……几乎完全覆了过来。

为什么要活着呢？

谁在乎。

身体像是灌了铅，四肢被看不见的东西困住，灵魂被分割的支离破碎。

宋郁昏沉之际，想起来那只在秋水巷撞过来的小鸟，温热的身躯，手指那些微微的啄感……

意识坠了下去。

与此同时，白粼粼已经在卧室门口鬼鬼祟祟了，他已经好些天没打游戏了。

鸟爱面子，鸟偷偷来打。

白粼粼先是探了探头，左右环顾了下，看到了“人”在床上睡觉才大摇大摆地往里面走。

啪嗒啪嗒的。

活脱脱一个走地鸡。

白粼粼扑棱翅膀飞到了椅子上，发现了耳机，里面还有游戏待机的声音，鸟很羡慕。

这个世界上不能研发一下给鸟用的耳机吗？小一号就行。
chunks.englishText:
"Parrots are actually omnivores, so it might be curious about human food. As for braised meat... didn't it eat that quite a while ago? If it's fine now, then it's fine."

Chen Kaihe was currently calling Song Yu from an archives center in S Province. His spirit was still high because the hospital had reported that Zhengguo's physical condition remained very stable, with a possibility of regaining consciousness.

Meanwhile, at Jinyuan, it was midnight.

Song Yu suffered from insomnia at night. Fresh out of the shower, his hair tips were still damp, and his facial features looked sharp under the desk lamp.

The rambling voice continued from the receiver:

"Scientific feeding is the right way, but little birds aren't that fragile either. Monk parakeets in South America peck at food discarded by humans too."

"Little Qi told me you bought it a lot of stuff? Have you named it yet?"

Chen Kaihe asked with warm affection. Since falling ill, Song Yu had become somewhat withdrawn, completely different from how he was as a child.

It was impossible for him not to feel heart-pained for the boy.

"No."

The night was deep. Song Yu looked down at the little bird in the tissue box, his heart calm.

Naming it...

"Alright, it's very late over there. Go to sleep early."

"I'm keeping watch here in S Province. Your grandfather is fine, so don't worry."

Chen Kaihe offered a few more gentle reminders before hanging up.

May arrived in the blink of an eye.

Song Yu had actually sought out the housekeeper a few times and given her a substantial amount of money. Initially, he had disliked how she constantly messaged Song Qiming, but after seeing her child in the hospital, he couldn't bring himself to say anything critical.

He gave her two hundred thousand yuan in total.

He claimed it was money for the bird's bibs.

Tears streamed down the auntie's face. In the end, she simply held Song Yu's hand, pleading with him to take care of himself and live well.

The youth had slit his wrists before.

Song Yu returned home in a dark mood. He didn't rehire the bird's "friend," even though he remembered seeing how happy the bird used to be around her.

It was now the holiday period, and with no one else in the villa, the house felt empty.

Walking over to the dining table, Song Yu couldn't help frowning: the bird food in the dish hadn't been touched at all.

Or rather, it had been nudged twice.

Just enough to make it look "touched."

The bird was perfunctorily faking it.

Song Yu felt flustered and troubled. He was trying to take good care of it, but real life never matched the online guides, leaving him lost as to what to do.

Right then, the sound of fluttering wings echoed from upstairs, and the little blue bird flew out from his bedroom.

It landed smoothly right on the "human's" shoulder.

Bai Linlin felt a bit guilty; he had just finished a round of gaming...

"Chirp chirp."

Song Yu lowered his eyes and cupped the bird in his hand, his expression darkening. The edges of the bird's feathers looked abnormal: along the shafts of those gorgeous blue feathers were horizontal dark-gray stripes.

Stress bars.

They could be caused by malnutrition or emotional distress.

Yet Qi Siyang had brought his junior fellow to conduct a full checkup, and the bird was completely healthy.

Which meant it was clearly the latter.

Bai Linlin's head was held lightly in place. He wiggled his short beak and began nibbling on the boy's hand—not hard, just gentle nips.

*Why hasn't he let go of me yet?*

Song Yu's emotional state turned terrible, but even so, he didn't vent any negative feelings at the bird. He merely touched its tiny head.

"Chirp chirp chirp?"

Bai Linlin tilted his head.

About an hour later, movers arrived at Jinyuan, carrying various items upstairs to one of the second-floor rooms.

Song Yu stood nearby, paying them and communicating instructions.

Having just finished a tour of the kitchen, the bird watched the people coming and going, pitter-pattering along the floor, unwilling to fly.

Looking just like a ground chicken.

"All settled, all paid up."

"Then we'll be taking off..."

The delivery crew turned to leave, but got a sudden start as they turned around: the bird was standing right on the floor, head tilted up to look at them, blocking the hallway.

Song Yu's expression softened. Crouching down, he offered his hand, and the bird naturally raised a leg, stepping up firmly.

*Mounting the chariot.*

"Sorry about that. It doesn't like cages, so it just roams around."

The workers nodded in understanding, though they couldn't help marveling as they walked away:

*These days, even birds get their own private rooms...*

Indeed, Song Yu had hired people to install a custom wooden climbing gym complete with various little treehouses, with the room's air conditioning running continuously.

Extremely luxurious.

Yet the outcome still wasn't great. The bird simply took a single lap around the room, grabbed a wheat straw in its beak, and flew back to land on Song Yu's shoulder.

Its round, plump head tilted.

And then it diligently stuck the wheat straw right into its own tail feathers.

Bai Linlin's reasoning was simple: he didn't have pockets, so he either had to hold it in his beak the whole time or stick it onto his feathers.

What he didn't expect was—

"Is it in heat?"

Song Yu had seen videos of birds tucking strips of paper into their tail feathers before. He had looked it up back then and found it was nest-building behavior.

Which mostly occurred in females.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!! Chirp chirp chirp!"

Bai Linlin's entire bird body overheated with rage. *What are you talking about?! What kind of wild accusations are those?!*

He squawked furiously in a burst of noise, bit Song Yu's hand with considerable force, and flew out the door.

Song Yu froze slightly. Blood trickled from his finger.

*It's so angry.*

*But I suppose that's normal. Hormonal mood swings during mating season...*

*Cute.*

Things didn't settle easily. Song Yu found that the bird was genuinely giving him the cold shoulder. The entire weekend, it refused to come near him,

Simply pitter-pattering around on the floor.

Looking like a fluffy ball.

Song Yu didn't know what to do; he had zero experience communicating with a little bird.

Especially when it hadn't eaten its bird food for days.

Song Yu was indeed beginning to spiral out of control. He barely ate anything himself, consumed by anxiety that the bird might die.

His mood sank into deep despondency.

In reality, Bai Linlin had no intention of going on a hunger strike whatsoever. He was completely familiar with the villa's layout and navigated to the snack stashes with ease.

The bird was round and chubby.

Not a single gram lighter.

He was just still super pissed!

*Song Yu is just a kid, how could he say something like that?!*

Although Bai Linlin possessed a bird's body, he still had the mind of an adult human. Being told he was "in heat"... felt practically like being flirted with.

As a lifelong single virgin, he needed several days to recover from the shock.

What he didn't know was that Song Yu had doubled his medication over this, to the point of suffering blurred vision.

Keeping a pet indeed helps with psychological regulation.

However, if the pet dies or rejects interaction, it backfires catastrophically.

Bai Linlin had completely forgotten that he hadn't touched his bird food, but in Song Yu's eyes, this was a hunger strike.

It was noon, and the bedroom door remained wide open.

Song Yu was playing games in his room, his face pale and cold. Screen after screen flashed past, and kill announcements echoed through the neckband headphones around his neck.

His heart pounded wildly, his vision blurring as dizziness took over.

*I can't raise it right.*

*I just can't raise anything right.*

Song Yu stood up and collapsed flat onto his back on the bed, covering his eyes with his hand. Black ink-like void swirled and writhed across his vision... almost completely engulfing him.

*Why go on living?*

*Who cares anyway.*

His body felt as heavy as lead, his limbs bound by invisible chains, his soul shattered into fragmented pieces.

As Song Yu slipped into unconsciousness, he recalled the little bird that had crashed into him back in Qiushui Alley—its warm little body, the soft nips against his fingers...

His consciousness plunged into the deep abyss.

At the same time, Bai Linlin was lurking suspiciously at the bedroom doorway. He hadn't played games for days.

*A bird has pride. Bird will play secretly.*

Bai Linlin first poked his head in, looking left and right. Only after seeing the "human" sleeping soundly on the bed did he waddle inside in a swaggering stride.

Pitter-patter, pitter-patter.

Looking for all the world like a ground chicken.

Bai Linlin flapped his wings and flew up onto the gaming chair, noticing the headphones emitting idle game sounds. The bird felt intensely envious.

*Can't someone in this world invent headphones designed for birds? Just one size smaller would be fine!*

chunks.chineseText:
不过他没有太浪费时间，而是伸了伸鸟腿，挪动了下鼠标，嚯，他战绩不错。

白粼粼一时半会入了神，火速开了一局，反正宋郁吃了药都会睡得很久的。

大不了一会立马飞走。

鸟开始紧张刺激地打游戏。

咳咳。

鸟时不时地回头看一眼床，有种偷情的感觉，身上的压力纹又深了一些。

但时局不利，白粼粼接连败北，但他又不甘心，只能再战，结果还是输。

鸟气得不行，合理怀疑是宋郁把胜率给打完了。

也就在这时，白粼粼的翅膀勾住了耳机线，一不小心给扯开了，游戏对局的背景音漏了出来。

但他已经杀红了眼。

完全没有注意到身后有被子被掀开的动静，只是一个劲地输出：

“啾啾啾，煞笔队友，不许挂机！”

“啾啾，去死啊！我一大炮轰死你。”

“艹啊！”

宋郁从床上坐直了身体，头发都被压翘了，只是面色恍惚。

白粼粼最后还是眼睁睁地看着水晶被推掉了，生气极了，一爪子踹了下鼠标，砰砰跳跳地回头。

“……”

“……”

作者有话说：

[鸽子]：人，可以当没有看到吗？

Ps:鹦鹉往自己尾羽上插纸条这个，我查过，多是牡丹鹦鹉，公的母的话，好像也都有。粼粼就单纯觉得叼着费劲，他就插自己尾羽上，不用深究
