Chapter 39 (Part 1)

The young man’s face flushed red. He was sitting cross-legged right on the other’s back, his shorts bunching up to reveal a pair of sleek, pale knees.

Bai Linlin was utterly flabbergasted. What his hands were propping him up on wasn’t the floor either… it was Song Yu’s back…

It felt so smooth.

Bai Linlin’s entire body grew piping hot. He scrambled to get down in a panic, but the person beneath him gave a soft chuckle.

And then did another push-up.

Down, then up.

It felt like riding a boat.

Fun as it was, it felt extremely bizarre.

Bai Linlin urgently tried to get down, even opening his mouth to blurt out in a flurry, “D-Don’t move!”

The youth was already reaching down with his arms, trying to find leverage to dismount, but Song Yu spoke up, turning his head slightly as he said, “It’s fine.”

“You can sit there.”

Bai Linlin’s heart hammered against his ribs. Thoroughly “cooked” from embarrassment, he shut his eyes and instantly transformed into a fluffy little bird, jumping right off the man’s back.

So mortified he scurried toward the door, pitter-pattering away.

Behind him came Song Yu’s voice: “Linlin?”

But the bird had already nimbly squeezed through the crack of the door, wings half-spread to vent off the heat.

-

It was around ten o’clock in the evening.

Only then did Song Yu finish his workout. He simply took a shower in the gym’s bathroom—a habit he had maintained over the past few days, as showering in the bedroom might disturb his little bird’s sleep.

Dressed in a black short-sleeved shirt, the young man reached out to pick up his phone. The light reflecting from the screen illuminated his exceptionally handsome face, featuring a straight nose and prominent brow bone.

Song Yu possessed cool, distant features that naturally gave off an aloof, unapproachable impression. Yet the moment his eyes fell upon his phone’s wallpaper, the chill in his gaze softened into tenderness.

The wallpaper was a close-up picture of a chubby little bird staring at the camera with its head tilted, bursting with vitality.

He looked at it for about half a minute before switching to a shopping app. It was filled with new snacks—after all, his little bird needed treats to share with its friends.

Song Yu bought fresh supplies every week.

Having taken care of that, he was about to head to the bedroom when his phone buzzed with several anonymous text messages:

[Song Yu, what do you mean by deleting your mother?]

[Are you trying to draw a line between us?]

[Do you have any idea that your grandfather destroyed my career? The old man used to distinguish right from wrong—what, did you go blow smoke in his ear?]

Song Yu stood at the doorway, looking down at the stream of incoming messages with pale, impassive features. His expression remained utterly calm.

[I know you hold a grudge against me... But did I ever leave you short on allowance? Did I give you any less than what Song Qiming gave you?]

Sometimes, Song Yu couldn't understand it either. Although his parents had been divorced for a long time, his mother seemed forever trapped in a state of endless comparison.

Was he short on money?

Both Song Qiming and Jiang Rui knew very well that he wasn't.

[Forget it. Either way, I'm leaving for Europe the day after tomorrow. If you...]

Song Yu turned off the screen. For a moment, he felt a faint dark smudge twisting before his eyes. After a second or two, he pushed the door open.

Everything returned to normal.

The bedroom was quiet. The desk lamp was still on, illuminating an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Song Yu walked over and touched it; it felt warm.

He turned his head to glance at the bed.

A plump little bird was lying on its side, putting on a grand act of being fast asleep, though its tiny claws were curled tightly into a ball.

Song Yu had originally wanted to walk over and check on his little bird, but worrying that it might feel awkward, he quietly backed out of the bedroom, closing the door as gently as possible.

Bai Linlin let out a long sigh of relief. His round bird head tilted stealthily to confirm the man had truly left before he sprang up with a leap, his claws leaving a deep dent in the pillow.

“...”

The bird felt a bit embarrassed.

Stretching its wings once more to release heat, Bai Linlin reflected. Having grown accustomed to being a bird, he often forgot he possessed a human soul inside, acting like a little king all day long. But ever since he learned how to shapeshift recently...

Problems seemed to have cropped up.

If he was a “human,” it didn't seem quite appropriate to sleep in the same bed, did it?

He couldn't treat someone as a free ride anymore either.

Nor could he strut into the bathroom to look for Song Yu without a second thought...

Bai Linlin felt inexplicably annoyed. Hanging his bird head in deep thought, he finally tucked his wings in and reached a furious conclusion:

Shapeshifting did more harm than good!

The bird took a total loss!

-

Downstairs in the tea room.

Song Yu had no intention of hiding the news he received. He simply felt he should inform his grandfather, while also... harboring a few thoughts of his own.

“I deleted Jiang Rui from my WeChat.”

The youth’s tone was calm. Looking at the only elder who truly cared for him, he asked softly, “Grandfather, was I wrong to do that?”

Song Zhengguo merely poured a cup of hot tea for the boy before him. Sharp-eyed and clear-headed as ever, the old man gently turned the question back to him: “Since you’re asking me, do you think it was right or wrong?”

Song Yu’s hanging fingers curled slightly. Drooping his eyelids, as if recalling something, he pinched his fingertip and murmured, “I’ve accepted the fact that my mother doesn’t love me.”

“It’s nothing really. I just want to sever this connection. After all these years...”

Song Yu suddenly let out a laugh—one tinged with self-mockery. Finding the scar on his wrist somewhat absurd, he simply added, “They’ve both built new families and stepped into new chapters of their lives, yet I’m still mired in the past... It isn’t fair.”

The youth repeated quietly, “It isn’t fair.”

“I want a completely new life too.”

The night was tranquil. In the end, grandfather and grandson did not dwell too long on the topic, shifting instead to company business and academic matters.

Seeing the child gradually walk out of the shadow, Song Zhengguo felt a deep sense of relief. Old as he was, he could still clear away a few troubles for the boy.

“Why did you choose Artificial Intelligence as your college major? I didn't ask you in detail last time. Would you like to tell your grandfather about it?”

The old man’s face was warm, his tone gentle and encouraging.

Song Yu froze for a moment upon hearing the question.

Noticing his reaction, Song Zhengguo explained further, “You’ve been too busy lately. Business administration isn't easy to study in the first place, and if you try to manage a cutting-edge field like AI on top of it... Child, I’m worried you’ll collapse from exhaustion.”

The atmosphere in the tea room was serene, wisps of white steam curling up from the purple-clay teapot.

Song Yu actually didn't know how to phrase it, because he had chosen that major back then simply to fulfill his little bird’s wish—

To install a front door with a footprint scanner for its little claws.

“...”

It really wasn't something easy to say out loud.

“Huabing is a massive corporation, and management is the most vital aspect. You will be taking the helm in the future. As for the direction of enterprise development—such as the emerging AI industry—you can simply create more positions, set up multiple studios, and let talented professionals put their skills to use...”

Song Zhengguo tried to put it more plainly: “Xiao Yu, you don't need to become a front-line engineer yourself. It’s too exhausting.”

Song Yu understood the reasoning. His academic workload was indeed overwhelming, and dropping one major would certainly relieve a great deal of pressure. But...

There was his little bird.

“Grandfather, I’ll think about it some more.”

The old man sighed softly. “You stubborn child...”

-

It was already past eleven when he returned to the bedroom. The bird was fast asleep, and the phone was plugged into its charger, displaying a five percent battery level.

Song Yu stood by the desk for a moment, then pulled a photo frame from the drawer. It had been delivered by property management a few days ago, and he had framed the photograph inside.

It was a picture of a little bird wearing a tiny Western cowboy hat and a matching harness, staring at the camera from a side profile.

A photo shoot.

Song Yu had taken the bird to a studio a while back, bringing along some custom outfits to shoot over a dozen sets of portraits, which cost about two thousand yuan.

It wasn't expensive at all.

Song Yu placed the small photo frame on the desk—a spot right at eye level whenever he looked up. A few months ago... this place had held a family portrait.

People always had to move forward.

He walked over to the bedside. Seeing the sleeping “youth,” he wasn't surprised in the slightest; it had been happening frequently lately.

chunks.chineseText:
会在梦里变成“人”。

宋郁撑着手臂看了一会，潮湿的黑发盖住了些眉眼，那颗红痣若隐若现的。

“粼粼？”

鸟睡着了。

“少年”蜷着身子，睡姿一般，甚至都没有枕到枕头上。

宋郁微微弯腰，抬手托起来床上“人”的后颈，想把“人”放到枕头上，但或许是动作还是有点吵醒它了。

“少年”一个歪头，把脸埋到了他的掌心。

不动了。

像是之前把鸟头插到他的手指之间的空隙一样。

宋郁呼吸都放轻了些，眼皮微微垂着，后面才慢慢地给放到了枕头上。

不过“少年”压住他的手了。

宋郁低头看了一会，没有再挣，只是抬手拿出来了手机，翻开微信里的联系人，找出来一只头像为鹤的“人”。

发送消息道：

[您好，我是编号247粼粼的监护人，我想问一下，它总是在睡觉的时候化成人形要紧吗？]

[对它身体健康会不会有影响？]

丹顶鹤其实在管理局正加班着的，上头说是南市来了个749局的人类，让管理局这边看顾好城市里的妖怪，尽可能地低调一些……

麻烦。

丹顶鹤拿着新到手的手机刷短视频，它的饲养员给他开了个账号，现在约莫有一万粉丝了。

嗯嗯。

不过就在这时消息弹出来了，它这次看了下，越看越满意。

247的监护人是真的不错。

多有礼貌。

说得清清楚楚的。

丹顶鹤心里好感度又往上涨了涨，然后才准备回消息。

宋郁这边还在床边，单手看手机的消息，另外一个手在给“少年”当枕头。

他侧眸一直看着，直到回复来了：

[人形吗？那其实不太常见，妖怪一般睡熟会倾向于保持自己原本的形态。]

[你观察一下吧，247毕竟是走歪门邪道上来的，根基不稳也正常。]

宋郁：“……”

他不觉得是歪门邪道。

他的小鸟很努力了。

但话不能这么说，宋郁还是同丹顶鹤道了谢，不过就在这时那边又发了几条消息：

[247这些天来基地总是不务正业，组织一堆小妖怪唱歌跳舞的，你让它好好做任务，提升等级有助于它稳定妖力，它还不到一岁，正是……]

总之是一大堆话。

宋郁还是不赞同。

他的小鸟不用努力。

不过他还是回复了句：

[好的，谢谢您。]

宋郁大概就这么保持一个动作有半个小时，“少年”才转了个身子，又沉沉地睡了过去。

他的手有些麻。

但更多的是一种温软的触感。

宋郁起身这才回了床的外侧，抬手刚把卧室的灯关了，脑海里却突然又浮现丹顶鹤发的那段话。

——睡熟会倾向于保持自己原本的形态。

是么？

-

翌日。

毛绒绒的小鸡神清气爽地醒了，啪嗒啪嗒就走到人的胸膛处，开始低头注视ing。

怎么还不醒？

白粼粼刚刚看手机了，今天是周末，宋郁不需要去学校和公司，而且现在已经八点钟了。

他没睡好吗？

鸟蓬了蓬毛，最后窝在人的锁骨处了，乖巧等待。

一会要去吃早饭。

有蟹黄包的。

白粼粼已经记住了家里的一周饮食，周末是福云阁的早茶，会有人送过来的。

鸟也要吃。

宋郁其实在梦里微微蹙了蹙眉，总觉得胸口有块小石头，沉沉的，等他睁开眼的时候……

身上的小鸟已经睡起了回笼觉，鸟头插在翅根里，一个蓝色毛球。

“……”

-

早餐大约是在八点半开始的，宋峥国在楼下看报纸，见到一人一鸟下来才温声道：

“怎么今天起晚了？”

“没睡好？”

宋郁还没来得及解释，肩头的小鸟就扑棱翅膀飞了过去，端端正正地站到了餐桌上。

那里有鸟的位置。

一个小盘子，里面是草莓块和小饼干，量很少，只是给小鸟尝个鲜。

旁边还有小围兜。

是阿姨新勾的，配套的蓝色，上面还有小白花。

鸟伸喙叼了起来，啪嗒啪嗒地走到老人的跟前。

宋峥国见状也不看宋郁了，只是很认真地接了过来，抬手去细致地给鸟儿系上，夸赞道：

“好好好，有仪式感。”

白粼粼美美地开始炫饭，反正人吃完桌上的东西是不会立即收的，按照规律来说，还会放个三十分钟。

很多天都是这样。

方便了鸟。

今天他就注意到了，根本就没有人吃蟹黄包！

简直是浪费！

宋峥国年纪大了本来胃口就不是很好，吃完就拿着报纸接着看，时不时地会看一眼桌上的小鸟。

圆滚滚的。

叨一口草莓看一口桌上的食物。

贪吃的鸟儿。

宋郁也在健身，其实没有吃太多，他要保持个好的身材，他的小鸟上次提过了。

“小郁，待会同我去下书房？”

宋峥国抬了抬眼，见人吃得差不多了才问道。

“好。”

后面祖孙俩就上楼去了，鸟当然没有跟上，白粼粼甚至还特地去目送他们关上门了。

很好。

鸟啪嗒啪嗒走到蟹黄包那里，直接把短喙伸进去了，鲜美的汤汁迸发在舌尖。

毛绒绒的翅膀都伸了伸。

爪子也打了点滑。

-

书房。

“爷爷这几天要出去一趟，在琅山那里的农家乐，跟你说一声。”

宋峥国面色很是温文尔雅，对着身边的少年说道。

“几天？您身体刚恢复没多久？我陪着吧。”

宋郁蹙了蹙眉，很不放心地问。

但老人只是摆了摆手，宽慰道：

“爷爷没事，只是我那位朋友，他性格古怪，不喜旁人跟着，也是有事才来南市的。”

宋峥国又想了想：

“你要说几天？爷爷也不大清楚……大概三五天？”

宋郁其实还想再说几句，但后面都被老人不动声色地推拒了，理由很多：一是认为琅山那里的农家乐是华秉的产业，很安全；二是说明自己身体素质不错，医生也说要多多活动。

“……”

宋郁也是没办法，最后只是道：

“那您记得和我通电话。”

也就在这时，门口处传来了爪子挠动的动静，嘎吱嘎吱的，很有劲。

宋峥国笑了笑，抬手让人去开门。

鸟就这么大摇大摆地进来了，喙上其实还沾了点汤汁，非常鲜香。

宋郁见到后一愣，随即就是采取行动，捏着那个小短喙，用指腹给拭掉了。

白粼粼还以为是拔河，一个劲地往后撤，结果人一松手，他直接啪唧坐在了地板上。

鸟：？

宋郁：“……”

白粼粼很是灵巧的一个弹跳，重新站了起来，收了收翅膀，很是大大方方地进来。

鸟很有家庭成员的自觉。

他们在聊什么具体的事？

有什么是鸟不能知道的？

白粼粼扑棱翅膀飞到了桌子上，稳稳当当地站在了笔筒上，开始表态。

“鸟儿吃完了？”

鸟闻言直接僵住。

“小草莓和小饼干。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 39 (Part 2)

He would transform into a “human” in his dreams.

Song Yu leaned down on one arm to watch for a moment. Damp black hair draped slightly over his brows, rendering the red mole on his forehead intermittently visible.

“Linlin?”

The bird was sound asleep.

The “youth” was curled up with poor sleeping posture, not even resting his head on the pillow.

Song Yu bent down slightly and reached out to cradle the back of the “youth’s” neck, intending to shift him onto the pillow. Perhaps the movement gently stirred him, however.

The “youth” tilted his head and buried his face right into Song Yu’s palm.

Then he stopped moving.

Just like how the little bird used to wedge its head into the gaps between his fingers.

Song Yu’s breathing softened slightly. With his eyelids lowered, he slowly eased the youth onto the pillow.

However, the “youth” was now resting right on top of his hand.

Song Yu looked down at him for a while, making no attempt to pull away. Instead, he reached out with his free hand to pick up his phone, scrolled through his WeChat contacts, and found a user whose profile picture was a red-crowned crane.

He sent a message:

[Hello, I am the guardian of Number 247, Linlin. May I ask if it is a problem that he constantly transforms into human form while sleeping?]

[Will it affect his health?]

The Red-Crowned Crane was actually working overtime at the Management Bureau. Word from above said someone from Bureau 749 in Nanshi had arrived, instructing the local bureau to keep a close eye on the city’s demons and stay as low-profile as possible...

What a headache.

The crane was swiping through short videos on its newly acquired phone. Its keeper had opened an account for it, which now had about ten thousand followers.

Mhm, not bad.

Just then, a message popped up. The crane glanced at it, growing increasingly pleased as it read.

247’s guardian was truly excellent.

So polite.

Explaining everything so clearly.

The crane’s favorable impression of him ticked up another notch before it prepped a reply.

Song Yu remained by the bedside, reading the message with one hand while using his other hand as a pillow for the “youth.”

He kept his gaze turned toward him until the reply arrived:

[Human form? That’s actually quite unusual. Demons generally prefer to maintain their original form when fast asleep.]

[Keep an eye on him. After all, 247 took a shortcut to gain enlightenment, so it’s normal for his foundation to be unstable.]

Song Yu: “...”

He didn't think it was taking a shortcut.

His little bird had worked very hard.

Still, he couldn't put it that way out loud, so Song Yu simply thanked the crane. However, several more messages immediately followed from the other side:

[These past few days at the base, 247 hasn't been attending to his proper duties at all. He’s been organizing a bunch of little demons to sing and dance. Tell him to do his tasks properly—raising his rank will help stabilize his demon force. He’s not even a year old yet, which is precisely the time...]

It was a mountain of nagging words.

Song Yu still disagreed.

His little bird didn't need to push itself so hard.

Nevertheless, he replied politely: [Understood, thank you.]

Song Yu maintained that position for about half an hour until the “youth” rolled over and drifted deeper into sleep.

His hand was somewhat numb.

Yet beneath it lingered a soft, warm sensation.

Song Yu stood up and returned to his side of the bed. Just as he switched off the bedroom light, the crane’s message suddenly popped back into his mind.

—*Demons generally prefer to maintain their original form when fast asleep.*

Was that so?

-

The next day.

The fluffy little chick woke up feeling refreshed and invigorated. Pitter-patter it waddled onto the man’s chest, staring down at him intently.

*Why isn't he awake yet?*

Bai Linlin had just checked his phone; today was the weekend, meaning Song Yu didn't need to go to school or the company, and it was already eight in the morning.

*Didn't he sleep well?*

The bird puffed out its feathers and finally nested at the crook of the man’s collarbone, waiting patiently.

They were going to have breakfast soon.

There would be crab roe buns.

Bai Linlin had already memorized the household’s weekly menu. Weekends meant dim sum from Fuyun Pavilion, delivered straight to their door.

The bird wanted to eat too.

Song Yu actually frowned slightly in his sleep, feeling a heavy little stone pressing against his chest. When he opened his eyes...

The little bird on top of him was taking a second nap, its bird head tucked neatly under its wing like a tiny blue fluffball.

“...”

-

Breakfast started around eight-thirty. Song Zhengguo was downstairs reading the newspaper. Seeing the young man and the bird come down, he asked warmly, “Why did you wake up so late today?”

“Didn't sleep well?”

Before Song Yu could explain, the little bird on his shoulder flapped its wings and flew over, perching neatly on the dining table.

There was a spot reserved for the bird.

A tiny plate containing strawberry chunks and tiny biscuits—a small portion just for the bird to enjoy a taste of fresh food.

Beside it lay a tiny bib.

It was newly crocheted by the housekeeper, matching in blue with little white flowers.

The bird picked it up with its beak and waddled over to the old man.

Seeing this, Song Zhengguo stopped looking at Song Yu entirely, carefully taking the bib and meticulously tying it around the bird’s neck, praising, “Good, good, very dignified.”

Bai Linlin happily began his feast. Either way, once the humans finished, the food on the table wouldn't be cleared away immediately; according to routine, it would sit there for thirty minutes.

It had been like this for many days.

Extremely convenient for the bird.

Today, he noticed that nobody was eating the crab roe buns at all!

What a utter waste!

Song Zhengguo didn't have much of an appetite due to his advanced age. After eating, he resumed reading his newspaper, glancing up occasionally at the little bird on the table.

Round and plump.

Taking a peck of strawberry, then stealing a glance at the dishes on the table.

What a gluttonous little bird.

Song Yu was working out lately, so he didn't eat much either, wanting to maintain a good physique—something his little bird had mentioned last time.

“Xiao Yu, will you come to the study with me in a bit?”

Song Zhengguo raised his eyes and asked once he saw the youth was nearly finished.

“Alright.”

Afterward, grandfather and grandson went upstairs. Naturally, the bird didn't follow; Bai Linlin even made a point of seeing them off until the door closed.

Wonderful.

The bird waddled over to the crab roe buns, thrusting his short beak straight inside as the savory, delicious broth burst across his tongue.

His fluffy wings stretched out in delight.

His little claws even slipped slightly on the table.

-

In the study.

“Grandfather needs to go out for a few days to a farmhouse resort at Mount Lang. I wanted to let you know,” Song Zhengguo said with a gentle expression to the youth beside him.

“For how many days? You only recovered a short while ago. Let me come with you,” Song Yu frowned, asking anxiously.

The old man simply waved a hand, reassuring him, “Grandfather is fine. It’s just that my friend has an eccentric personality and dislikes being accompanied by extra people. He only came to Nanshi because of some business.”

Song Zhengguo thought for a moment. “If you ask how many days... Grandfather isn't quite sure either... Probably three to five days?”

Song Yu wanted to press further, but the old man smoothly deflected his concerns with various reasons: first, the farmhouse resort at Mount Lang was part of Huabing’s assets and entirely safe; second, his health was quite good, and the doctor had recommended getting plenty of light exercise.

“...”

Song Yu had no choice but to say, “Then remember to call me.”

Right at that moment, a scratching sound came from the door—*creak, creak*—quite vigorous and energetic.

Song Zhengguo smiled and signaled for the youth to open the door.

The bird strutted right in, its beak visibly smeared with a bit of savory broth.

Song Yu froze upon seeing it, then immediately moved into action, pinching the tiny short beak to wipe it clean with his thumb.

Bai Linlin thought they were playing tug-of-war and kept pulling backward. As soon as the man let go, he plopped right onto his bottom on the floor.

Bird: ?

Song Yu: “...”

Bai Linlin bounced back up with a nimble leap, tucking his wings back in and walking further inside with absolute composure.

The bird possessed a keen sense of being a core family member.

What were they discussing so secretly?

Was there anything a bird shouldn't know?

Bai Linlin flapped his wings and flew onto the desk, perching solidly atop the pen holder to make his presence known.

“Is the bird done eating?”

Hearing that, the bird froze instantly on the spot.

“Your little strawberries and biscuits.”

chunks.chineseText:
白粼粼这才定了定心，很矜持地点了点头。

宋峥国这才爽朗一笑，转而认真地道：

“爷爷要出门几天，鸟儿在家好好吃饭？”

白粼粼这才歪了歪头，要出门？

去哪里？

鸟扑棱翅膀下来了，在书桌上刚啪嗒啪嗒走几步就被宋郁给拿起来了，被迫站在了他的肩头。

少年只是认真问：

“琅山那里的工作人员知道您要去的事吗？我交代一下吧……”

“也是，我真是老了，这个都忘了。”

后面就是一些琐碎的注意事项，其实没有什么意思，白粼粼当成背景音了。

鸟专注地看书房墙上挂着的“画作”，其实原来这个地方是有一个“天道酬勤”的书法作品的，不过现在变成一幅花鸟画。

主角显而易见，是一只毛绒绒的蓝羽小鸟。

白粼粼很满意。

这个家，果然是离不开鸟的！

-

时间又推移了几天，宋峥国也抵达了琅山的一个“农家乐”。

但说是“农家乐”，其实更像是度假村，不仅风景秀丽，里面的设施也一应俱全。

“好久不见，峥国，你最近怎么样？”

对面坐着的是个道士，穿着一身八卦祥云道袍，头发也是花白，个子不高，但看着眼睛黑亮有神。

现下正拿筷子吃着牛肉片，眉眼都舒坦开了，活脱脱一个精神小老头的样子。

“我想着你这次来南市，正好问你点事……是这样。”

宋峥国犹豫了下，斟酌道：

“我有一个朋友……”

对面的人筷子一顿，抬眼看了过来，一副我看你怎么编的样子。

“……”

宋峥国没有办法，只能把事情的来龙去脉说了，但对面的小老头只是摆手道：

“你是不是看错了，或许那就是个人，不过是你孙子藏起来了，后面让人家走了而已。”

“不要封建迷信啊。”

身着道袍的人语气认真，把一盘子肉炫光了。

宋峥国只是道：“我既然撞见了，那不可能不查。”

“物业的监控我也看了，家里没有人第三人出来，房间我也一一找了，属实是没有。”

老人只是叹了口气，只是道：

“我后面看了家里近一周的监控，依然是没有，平云，我是真的只能往那里想……”

道士这才吃完，擦了擦嘴，这一路奔波的，终于投奔到宋家了。

小老头只是问：

“是让我收了它吗？”

-

宋郁后面也没有去送江芮，只是发了一句“一路顺风”，后面就把那些收到的短信全部删了。

他心情其实不是很好，以至于从学校早早地就回来了，但刚一开门，两只毛绒绒的小鸟就在挤在一起看电影，还是恐怖的那种。

宋郁进门的时候正好播放到惊悚场面，房间里响起来此起彼伏的“啾啾啾啾啾！”

很聒噪。

“……”

灰棕色小雀甚至把头放在了蓝羽小鸟的翅膀下，001觉得画面太恐怖了。

虽然它也叨过眼球之类的。

白粼粼看到宋郁回来了，熟练地用爪子踩了下鼠标，把电影给暂停了，仰头就看了过去。

“宋郁！”

少年抬步走了过去，很温和地伸了手指，鸟立即抬腿上来，一顿攀爬抵达肩头。

“打游戏打游戏。”

“001，你快过来看，学一学！”

宋郁听着自家小鸟骄傲的语气，不由得笑了下，那些负面情绪也消散了，只是照做打开了游戏。

开始操作。

肩头有两只毛绒绒的小鸟在聚精会神地看着。

-

而与此同时，琅山这里。

“那你又没有这个想法……看来这是个段位很高的妖怪了？”

道士想了想，又问：

“它是不是会蛊惑人心？”

宋峥国脑海里浮现小鸟板板正正地站着，鸟眼圆圆地看着他的样子。

“……应该？”

道士点了点头，明了，又排查：

“有没有对鲜血反应大？”

“嗜血如命吗？”

宋峥国：“……”

嗜蟹黄包如命。

-

宋郁就这么一直打到了晚上，肩头的小鸟也只剩下了一只，蓝羽小鸟困困的，后面就往他肩头挪，蓬毛，开始睡下了。

他的确不能理解。

江芮为什么认为是他吹耳边风……

他吹什么风？

他控诉什么？

宋郁还是会被影响到一些，直到怀里多了个睡着的“少年”，面对面地抱着，浅蓝色的头发甚至碰到了他的下巴，有痒痒的触感。

鸟睡着了。

又恢复成人形了。

宋郁愣了下，把游戏关了，只是抬手揽着那截腰，抱着，什么也没做。

他的小鸟特别爱美。

一天要换两套衣服，上午是走的极繁主义，身上叮叮咣咣的，戴了好多配饰；下午天气有些变冷，换成了长袖长裤，都是纯棉材质的，咖色的卫衣衬得“少年”的皮肤更白。

宋郁都是在它睡着的时候看到的，不然也不知道要换好几次。

他抬手勒了下那截腰，微微低头……

“唔。”

怀里“人”就发出这么个不舒服的气音，宋郁一夜都没有再动过了，硬生生地这么维持着抱着的姿势，让他的小鸟安眠。

-

但这样的后果就是，人生病了。

不仅仅是一夜着凉，还有前段时间连轴转，以及江芮那些匿名短信……总之是这些因素堆积到了一起。

身体开始罢工。

但就算如此，宋郁早上还是单手抱着“人”去了床上，本意是让他的小鸟再睡会儿，顺手也叫了祥云阁的早茶外送，备注了蟹黄包要新鲜的。

白粼粼其实醒过来的时候就觉得有些不对劲了，但他还是听话去吃早饭了，宋郁似乎没什么胃口，只是说要去睡一觉。

鸟有些担心。

他把美食放在一旁了，啪嗒啪嗒地在人身后跟着。

宋郁上楼也没有发现，顺手关卧室门的时候鸟从善如流地钻了进来。

之后就是躺在了床上，他昏睡了过去。

白粼粼扑棱翅膀上去了，很认真地伸着鸟头过去，抵了下。

很热。

他发烧了。

鸟担心，鸟着急。

鸟不能去打电话，因为他只是一个小鸟。

白粼粼在地板上来回转，最后没办法，只能啪嗒啪嗒地朝着洗手间那里走，用爪子打开水龙头，叼着毛巾浸湿，然后捞了出来……

毛绒绒的小鸡在地板上来回走，伸着翅膀维持平衡。

-

宋峥国提前回来了，原因是他觉得鸟儿不算什么坏妖怪，为什么要收了？

思来想去还是婉拒了朋友过来拜访的要求。

鸟儿又不会害小郁。

老人想到这里，不由得想去看看自己孙子，毕竟华秉那里说这孩子今天没来，估摸着是身体不舒服了。

宋峥国直接去了二楼的卧室那里，见门半开着，索性就抬手推开了。

也就在这时——

里面那个浅蓝色头发的少年出现了，“他”正蹲在床边，身着白色衬衫和黑色短裤，正眼巴巴地看着床上的人。

听到了门口的动静才回了头。

作者有话说：

[鸽子][鸽子]：史诗级会面！
chunks.englishText:
Bai Linlin finally calmed down and nodded with a reserved air.

Song Zhengguo gave a hearty chuckle before turning serious:

"Grandpa's going away for a few days. Make sure you eat well at home, little bird, alright?"

Bai Linlin tilted his head. *Going away? Where to?*

Flapping his wings, the bird descended. He had only taken a few pitter-patter steps across the desk before Song Yu scooped him up, forcing him to perch on his shoulder.

The youth simply asked in earnest, "Do the staff at Mount Lang know you're coming? Let me drop them a line..."

"True, true. I really am getting old, forgetting something like that."

What followed were trivial instructions and reminders, which weren't particularly interesting, so Bai Linlin treated them as background noise.

The bird focused his attention on the "artwork" hanging on the study wall. Originally, a piece of calligraphy reading *Heaven Rewards the Diligent* had hung there, but now it had been replaced by a flower-and-bird painting.

The main subject was painfully obvious: a fluffy little blue-feathered bird.

Bai Linlin was very satisfied.

*This home truly cannot function without a bird!*

-

A few days passed, and Song Zhengguo arrived at an "agritourism farmstay" at Mount Lang.

Though called a "farmstay," it was more like a luxury resort, boasting not only breathtaking scenery but also top-notch, fully equipped facilities.

"Long time no see, Zhengguo. How have you been lately?"

Sitting across from him was a Taoist priest dressed in a robe adorned with Eight Trigrams and auspicious clouds. He had graying hair and was short in stature, but his dark eyes sparkled with vitality.

At the moment, he was picking up sliced beef with his chopsticks, his expression thoroughly relaxed—the very picture of a lively, spirited old man.

"I knew you were coming to Nanshi this time, so I thought I'd ask you about something... It goes like this."

Song Zhengguo hesitated, carefully phrasing his words: "I have a friend..."

The person opposite paused his chopsticks and looked up, his expression practically saying, *Let's see how you spin this tale.*

"..."

Left with no alternative, Song Zhengguo explained the whole sequence of events from start to finish. However, the little old man simply waved his hand dismissively:

"Are you sure you didn't just missee? Maybe it was a real person, but your grandson hid them away and let them leave later."

"Don't go engaging in superstitious nonsense."

The man in the Taoist robe spoke in a solemn tone while effortlessly polishing off the entire plate of meat.

Song Zhengguo simply said, "Since I stumbled upon it myself, there's no way I won't investigate."

"I checked the property management's surveillance footage, and no third person ever left the house. I searched every single room, and there truly was nobody."

The old man sighed and added, "I later checked the house's security footage for the entire past week, and still found nothing. Pingyun, I really have no choice but to suspect supernatural causes..."

Only then did the priest finish eating and wipe his mouth. After traveling all this way, he had finally made it to the Song family's hospitality.

The little old man asked flatly, "So, do you want me to exorcise it?"

-

Song Yu did not end up seeing Jiang Rui off. He merely sent a simple "Safe travels" text and deleted all the messages he had received from her.

He was in a rather low mood, which led him to return home early from school. But as soon as he opened the door, he found two fluffy little birds huddled together watching a movie—a horror film, no less.

Right as Song Yu walked in, a jump scare played on screen, causing a barrage of shrill "Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!" to echo through the room.

It was overwhelmingly noisy.

"..."

The ash-brown sparrow even tucked its head under the blue-feathered bird's wing. 001 found the visuals far too terrifying—even though it had pecked at things like eyeballs before.

Seeing that Song Yu was back, Bai Linlin deftly stepped on the mouse with his claw to pause the movie, then tilted his head up to look at him.

"Song Yu!"

The youth walked over and gently extended a finger. The bird immediately stepped onto it and clambered all the way up to his shoulder.

"Play games, play games!"

"001, come over and watch! Learn a thing or two!"

Listening to his bird's proud tone, Song Yu couldn't help but chuckle. The negative emotions dissipated, and he complied by launching the game, starting to play.

Two fluffy little birds perched on his shoulder, watching with rapt attention.

-

Meanwhile, at Mount Lang.

"So you don't want me to exorcise it... Sounds like this demon is pretty high-level then?"

The Taoist priest pondered for a moment before asking, "Can it bewitch human minds?"

The image of the little bird standing primly and proper, staring at him with round, glossy eyes, floated into Song Zhengguo's mind.

"...Probably?"

The priest nodded in understanding, continuing his diagnosis: "Does it react strongly to fresh blood?"

"Is it bloodthirsty?"

Song Zhengguo: "..."

*It's crab-roe-steamed-bun-thirsty.*

-

Song Yu kept playing until evening came. Only one bird remained on his shoulder now; the blue-feathered bird was drowsy, inching closer toward his neck, puffing out its feathers, and drifting off to sleep.

He truly couldn't understand why Jiang Rui assumed he was whispering poison into his grandfather's ear... What poison? What was he even accusing her of?

Song Yu was still somewhat bothered by it all—until a sleeping "youth" suddenly filled his arms. They were holding each other face-to-face, the youth's light blue hair tickling his chin with a gentle, itchy sensation.

The bird had fallen asleep and reverted to human form.

Song Yu paused, shut off the game, and simply wrapped his arm around that slender waist, holding him without doing anything else.

His little bird was exceedingly fond of looking good. He changed outfits twice a day: in the morning, he went for a maximalist style, clinking and clanking with numerous accessories; in the afternoon, as the weather grew cooler, he switched to a long-sleeved top and pants made of pure cotton. The coffee-colored hoodie made the youth's skin look even fairer.

Song Yu only noticed these things while the bird was asleep; otherwise, he wouldn't even have known about the multiple wardrobe changes.

He pulled that slender waist a little tighter and slightly lowered his head...

"Mm..."

The "person" in his arms let out a soft, discontented puff of air. Song Yu didn't move for the rest of the night, stubbornly holding that exact pose to let his little bird sleep peacefully.

-

However, the consequence of doing so was that he fell ill.

It wasn't just catching a chill overnight, but also the cumulative toll of working non-stop recently, combined with Jiang Rui's anonymous text messages... All these factors piled up together.

His body finally went on strike.

Even so, Song Yu carried the "person" to bed with one arm in the morning, intending to let his little bird sleep a bit longer. He also ordered morning dim sum delivery from Xiangyun Pavilion, adding a note that the crab roe buns had to be fresh.

When Bai Linlin woke up, he felt something was off, but he obediently went to eat breakfast. Song Yu didn't seem to have much of an appetite, saying he just wanted to get some sleep.

The bird grew worried. Setting the delicious food aside, he pitter-pattered after him.

Song Yu didn't notice as he walked upstairs, and when he casually closed the bedroom door, the bird smoothly slipped inside.

After lying down on the bed, Song Yu fell into a feverish stupor.

Bai Linlin flapped his wings and landed on the bed, earnestly poking his tiny bird head forward to press against Song Yu's forehead.

Very hot. He had a fever.

The bird was worried; the bird was anxious. But the bird couldn't make a phone call because he was just a little bird.

Bai Linlin paced back and forth across the floor. In the end, having no other choice, he pitter-pattered toward the bathroom, used his claws to turn on the faucet, grabbed a towel in his beak to soak it, and pulled it out...

The fluffy little creature walked back and forth across the floor, extending his wings to keep his balance.

-

Song Zhengguo returned earlier than planned because he realized that the little bird wasn't a bad demon—so why exorcise it?

After thinking it over, he politely declined his friend's offer to visit. The bird wouldn't hurt Xiao Yu anyway.

At this thought, the old man decided to check on his grandson, especially since Hua Bing had mentioned the boy hadn't shown up today, likely feeling under the weather.

Song Zhengguo went straight to the second-floor bedroom. Finding the door half-ajar, he simply pushed it open.

Right at that moment—

The youth with light blue hair was right there. "He" was squatting by the bed, wearing a white shirt and black shorts, gazing anxiously at the person lying in bed.

Hearing the noise at the door, he finally turned his head.

[Pigeon][Pigeon]: An epic encounter!

chunks.chineseText:
第40章

时间仿佛静止了。

宋峥国纵然是再见识多，也还是不由得后退了一步，这……他没想到会这么直接撞见。

对面的“少年”也是先一愣，后面就是惶恐，猛地转过去了头，留下一个毛绒绒的后脑勺。

宋峥国想了想，当机立断走出了卧室，直接砰得一声把门给关上了。

没事，没事，只要鸟儿恢复原貌……他就当没看见。

“……”

老人也是心里砰砰跳，在门口开始踱步，脑海里不断浮现刚刚那“少年”的脸。

就巴掌大，肤色还很白。

生的……的确好看。

宋峥国想到这里愣了下，想起来一件事来，面色变得有些复杂。

原来……是只小公鸟。

-

门内的“少年”早就慌得不行了，他没有经历过这种事，一下子站了起来，几乎本能地看向床上的“人”。

想叫人。

但又想起来对方生病了。

白粼粼只好砰得一下变回小鸟，但是他看了看门口，又低着鸟头看了看自己的翅膀……

这不坐实了他是鸟变的？

不行不行。

白粼粼脑子高速运转，想起来宋郁说过的事……对象，他是对象……那爷爷是见过他的。

他有身份的！

鸟一着急，立马又幻化成人，不过这次他还没有来得及组织语言，门就又开了。

宋峥国站在门口，其实是愣了下的，这怎么……

还没变回去？

“少年”站在床边，背着手，视线都在回避，往后退了一小步，又似乎是鼓足勇气，开口想要说什么。

但就在这时——

宋峥国说了句：“鸟儿？”

白粼粼天塌了。

浅蓝色的发尾甚至都不翘了，“少年”面色都变红了，连着后退了好几步。

他被发现了。

宋峥国后知后觉自己不该这么问，但是已经晚了，面前的“少年”砰得一下化成小鸟，扑棱翅膀就飞到了床上，一个劲地往床上人的肩窝钻，毛绒绒的，爪子都在用力。

最后成功地拱到被子里了。

只留下来一点点尾羽。

没动静了。

开始装死。

“……”

宋峥国看了下卧室的情况，发现床头柜那里放着一杯热水，旁边有翻出来的退烧药，窗户开了点缝隙，保证新鲜空气的流通但不会冷到，地板也是刚拖过的，因为还有着未干的水痕……

至于床上的人，老人走过去看了下，宋郁的额头上盖着湿毛巾，拧干的那种。

“……”

或许是被窝里的某只听到了脚步声，又努力地往里拱了拱。

宋峥国看了过去，发现一点尾羽都没有了，全钻进去了。

他有些担心，这不闷么？

卧室里安安静静的。

宋峥国想了想，觉得自己吓到了它了，试着开口道：

“鸟儿？”

“你别怕。”

被窝里的凸起一开始还没有动静，后面像是被说动了，偷偷地用爪子踹开一点被子，在里面掉了个头……

很谨慎地探出鸟头。

对视ing。

宋峥国松了口气，心想可以沟通也是好的，但是刚一开口：“爷爷不是……”

嗖！

鸟头立马钻回了被子里。

速度非常之快。

再度装死。

“……”

-

宋郁是在九点半的时候清醒的，他朦朦胧胧地觉得下巴处有点痒，后面又听到一些交谈声。

“是，应该是发烧了。”

“那可能需要挂水，这样起效比较快……”

宋郁渐渐睁开了眼，视野也逐步地清晰了起来，侧了侧头，看到了房间里的情况：

家庭医生在拿着医疗包，正在调试针剂，注意到目光后才对身后的老人说：

“宋老先生，孩子醒了。”

宋郁撑着身子坐了起来，面色其实有些苍白，但是他刚想说话，肩窝的毛绒绒就开始往下滑……

他愣了下。

抬手掀开了被子。

鸟圆滚滚的，像个毛球一样窝在床单上，被发现后就啪嗒啪嗒又要往被子里面走，很是着急的样子。

宋郁抬手握住了，放到了自己肩头，侧眸问：

“怎么了？”

旁边的医生看到后抬了抬眉，说了几句：

“养了小鸟啊？”

“这么亲人。”

宋郁很温和地对医生点了下头，说道：

“是，我的小鸟。”

宋峥国抬步走了过来，视线其实是先落在孙子肩头上的小鸟的，但是对方正在专注地歪头梳理羽毛，于是只能作罢。

转而去问宋郁：

“小郁，你发烧了知道不知道？”

少年确实没办法为自己辩白，张了张口，最后只是道：

“我想着睡一觉就好了。”

“不过爷爷你怎么这么早回来了？”

宋郁其实并没有发现什么异常，他还是照旧地同自己爷爷沟通，顺带伸出去了手背，血管处有轻微的刺痛，粗针扎了进去，有微凉的液体输入。

“我那老友他后面说有事，已经来市区了，所以就不待在琅山那里了。”

宋峥国说完这话，背着手在卧室里来回走动着，虽说是看着吊瓶的液体容量，但实际上目光一直在偷偷看鸟。

“爷爷？”

宋峥国闻言立马站直了身子，咳嗽了两声，摆了摆手说“没事”。

但少年不这么觉得，他说完那话就侧头看了下肩头的那只，鸟已经梳理羽毛有十几分钟了。

“……”

怎么了？

-

与此同时，管理局内。

丹顶鹤这次选择了非常优雅的藏蓝色丝带，在“工作室”内调整了一下位置，又询问了下旁边的杜宾：

“怎么样，可以吧？”

兽头人身的杜宾点了点头，又看了看手表的时间，提醒道：

“时间差不多了。”

丹顶鹤推开了“工作室”的门，以它为首，两侧有着一堆各色各样的妖怪，虽然都保持着一些人类的装扮，但都留有自己本体的特征。

它们具有化形的能力，但更以自己的物种自豪。

先是优雅从容的狸花猫，伸着自己的美甲细细品味；后面是一只戴着墨镜的眼镜王蛇，很从容地半直立爬行；最后则是一只戴着蝴蝶结发箍的角蛙，在后面蹦蹦跳跳的……

这些都是窗口的负责人。

由于丹顶鹤能说会道，所以被派为代表，而大厅的正前方，有一扇门打开了，一队西服革履的鼠鼠也严阵以待，请过来了后面的人。

一个穿着道袍的老头子。

对视。

丹顶鹤很是优雅地伸了下翅膀，平和地道：

“请。”

城市毕竟是人类建立起来的，妖怪管理局处在人流密集处，且近年化形的妖怪数量剧增，其实是有些反常的。

灵气涌动得太频繁了。

749局关注到了这个现象，并且开始定期派遣专员来地方视察，主要是来妖怪管理局查看登记在册的档案。

一来判断妖怪数量，二来看管理局是否尽职。

而面前这个道士，就是今年749局的“专员”。

丹顶鹤它们带着这个人类去了“会议室”，那是个长长的桌子，背景上有金纹流动，很是富丽堂皇。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 40

Time seemed to freeze.

No matter how experienced Song Zhengguo was, he couldn't help taking a step back. This... he hadn't expected to bump into the truth so head-on.

The "youth" opposite him was similarly stunned at first, followed by sheer panic. He abruptly turned his head away, leaving only the back of his fluffy head visible.

Song Zhengguo thought fast and decisively stepped out of the bedroom, slamming the door shut with a loud *thud*.

It was fine, it was fine. As long as the bird transformed back into its original form... he could pretend he had seen nothing at all.

"..."

The old man's heart pounded in his chest as he paced outside the door, the image of that "youth's" face constantly flashing in his mind.

It was only the size of a palm, and the skin was exceptionally fair.

He was... truly good-looking.

Song Zhengguo paused at the thought, realizing something that caused his expression to turn somewhat complex.

So... it was a little male bird.

-

Inside the room, the "youth" was already frantic. Having never experienced anything like this before, he scrambled to his feet and instinctively looked toward the person on the bed.

He wanted to call out for help.

Then he remembered that Song Yu was sick.

Bai Linlin had no choice but to pop back into his little bird form with a soft *poof*. But looking toward the door, and then lowering his head to inspect his own wings...

Didn't this just confirm that he was a bird that could shape-shift?

No, no, no!

Bai Linlin's mind raced as he recalled what Song Yu had said... Partners. He was Song Yu's partner... which meant Grandpa had met him before.

He had a legitimate identity!

In his panic, the bird instantly shape-shifted back into human form. However, before he could organize his words, the door opened once again.

Song Zhengguo stood at the doorway, utterly bewildered. How come...

He hadn't changed back?

The "youth" stood by the bed with his hands behind his back, avoiding eye contact as he shrank back a step. Then, as if plucking up all his courage, he opened his mouth to say something.

Just then—

Song Zhengguo blurted out, "Birdie?"

Bai Linlin felt as if the sky had fallen.

The tips of his light blue hair stopped perkily curling up. The "youth's" face flushed red, and he stumbled back several steps.

He was busted!

Song Zhengguo realized a moment too late that he shouldn't have asked like that, but the damage was done. With a soft *poof*, the "youth" before him turned back into a tiny bird. Flapping his wings, he flew straight onto the bed and squeezed himself furiously into the crook of the sick youth's shoulder. His fluffy body wriggled with all its might, claws working overtime.

Finally, he successfully burrowed into the blanket.

Only a tiny bit of tail feathers remained visible.

Silence fell.

He began playing dead.

"..."

Song Zhengguo surveyed the bedroom. He noticed a cup of warm water on the nightstand, next to some fever medicine that had been pulled out. The window was cracked slightly open to ensure fresh air circulation without letting in a draft. The floor had just been mopped, still bearing faint wet streaks...

As for the person in bed, the old man walked over to check. Song Yu had a damp, wrung-out towel resting on his forehead.

"..."

Perhaps hearing footsteps, the little lump under the blanket worked even harder to burrow inward.

Song Zhengguo glanced over and noticed that even the tail feathers had disappeared—the bird had completely tucked himself inside.

He felt a bit worried. *Won't he suffocate in there?*

The bedroom was dead quiet.

Song Zhengguo thought for a moment and realized he must have frightened the little creature. He tried speaking in a gentle voice:

"Birdie?"

"Don't be afraid."

The bulge under the blanket showed no reaction at first. Then, as if persuaded, a claw secretly kicked open a slit in the blanket, and the bird turned around inside...

He cautiously poked his tiny bird head out.

They locked eyes.

Song Zhengguo let out a sigh of relief, thinking it was good that they could communicate. But the moment he opened his mouth to say, "Grandpa didn't mean to..."

*Whoosh!*

The bird head instantly retracted into the blanket.

It was blindingly fast.

Back to playing dead.

"..."

-

Song Yu regained consciousness around nine-thirty. He felt a vague tickle against his chin and faintly heard voices conversing nearby.

"Yes, it seems to be a fever."

"An IV drip would be best. It'll take effect faster..."

Song Yu gradually opened his eyes, his vision clearing step by step. He turned his head and surveyed the room.

The family doctor was holding a medical bag, preparing a syringe. Noticing Song Yu's gaze, he turned to the old man behind him:

"Elder Song, the boy is awake."

Song Yu propped himself up into a sitting position. His face was still quite pale, but just as he was about to speak, a fluffy bundle in the crook of his shoulder began sliding downward...

He paused.

Lifting the blanket, he looked down.

The bird was round and plump, curled up like a fur ball on the bedsheet. Upon being discovered, he panicked and began pitter-pattering away, trying desperately to dive back under the covers.

Song Yu reached out, gently cupping the bird in his hand before setting him on his shoulder. Turning his head, he asked:

"What's wrong?"

The doctor nearby raised an eyebrow and remarked with a smile:

"You're raising a bird?"

"It's so attached to you."

Song Yu nodded politely at the doctor and said softly:

"Yes, he's my little bird."

Song Zhengguo stepped closer. His eyes originally landed on the tiny bird perched on his grandson's shoulder, but the creature was currently intent on tilting its head and preening its feathers, so the old man had to give up.

Instead, he turned to ask Song Yu:

"Xiao Yu, did you know you had a fever?"

The youth truly had no defense for himself. He parted his lips, ultimately saying:

"I thought I'd be fine after a night's sleep."

"Though, Grandpa, why did you come back so early?"

Song Yu didn't notice anything amiss, conversing with his grandfather as usual. He extended his hand; a slight prick hit his vein as a thick needle went in, followed by the cool sensation of fluid flowing into his system.

"My old friend had something come up and went straight to the city, so we didn't stay at Mount Lang."

After saying this, Song Zhengguo paced back and forth in the bedroom with his hands behind his back. Though he appeared to be monitoring the fluid levels of the IV bag, his eyes were constantly sneaking glances at the bird.

"Grandpa?"

Song Zhengguo immediately straightened up, cleared his throat with a couple of coughs, and waved his hand dismissively: "It's nothing."

The youth didn't quite believe it. After speaking, he turned his head to look at the bird on his shoulder. The bird had been preening its feathers for over ten minutes now.

"..."

*What was going on?*

-

Meanwhile, at the Demon Management Bureau.

The Red-crowned Crane spirit had chosen an extraordinarily elegant navy-blue ribbon today. Standing in the "studio," it adjusted its posture and asked the Doberman next to it:

"How is it? Does this look alright?"

The beast-headed, human-bodied Doberman nodded, checked the time on his wristwatch, and reminded:

"It's about time."

The Crane spirit pushed open the "studio" door. Leading the way, it was followed by a variety of demons on either side. Though they all wore human clothes, they retained the distinct features of their true forms.

They possessed the ability to shape-shift, but took immense pride in their respective species.

First came an elegant and composed Calico Cat spirit, carefully inspecting her manicured claws; behind her was a King Cobra spirit wearing sunglasses, slithering along in a grand, semi-upright posture; bringing up the rear was a Horned Frog spirit wearing a bow headband, hopping cheerfully behind...

These were all the heads of the service counters.

Because the Crane spirit was articulate and persuasive, it had been appointed as the representative. In front of the main hall, a door opened, and a team of suit-and-tie-clad Mouse spirits stood at the ready, respectfully ushering in the person behind them.

It was an old man wearing a Taoist robe.

Their eyes met.

The Crane spirit gracefully extended a wing and said serenely:

"Please, this way."

After all, modern cities were built by humans. The Demon Management Bureau was located in a densely populated area, and the recent surge in shape-shifting demons was rather abnormal.

Spiritual energy was fluctuating far too frequently.

Bureau 749 had taken notice of this phenomenon and begun periodically dispatching special commissioners to local branches for inspections, mainly to review the registered personnel files at the Demon Management Bureau.

This served two purposes: first, to gauge the demon population, and second, to check if the Bureau was fulfilling its duties.

And the Taoist priest standing before them was this year's "special commissioner" from Bureau 749.

The Crane spirit and its team led the human into a "conference room." It featured a long table set against a magnificent backdrop flowing with shimmering golden patterns, radiating immense opulence and grandeur.

chunks.chineseText:
道士老头看了下自己的手机，果不其然没有信号，这里的“界”是由妖怪们控制的。

749局虽然名义上可以“视察”，但妖怪管理局也做出了规定，只允许单独的人类进入基地。

算是一种微妙的抗衡。

“为什么现在妖怪的数量越来越多了？”

道士声音中气十足的，环着手臂就是质问，他是真的觉得有问题。

妖界还研发出了什么津贴制……那是怎么弄出来的？

丹顶鹤不卑不亢地道：

“灵气复苏而已，少见多怪。”

道士：“……”

“那大量妖怪聚集在城市，本来就很不合理，妖怪就应该回归山林！”

丹顶鹤闻言很是生气，直接伸翅膀拍桌子了，义正词严地道：

“什么叫回归山林？世界只是你们人类的世界吗？山林……山林不全被你们砍伐了吗？”

“我们很多同族都无家可归！”

道士这次做了充足的准备，从包里拿出来相关的文件说明，一把拍了过去：

“请看！”

“我国植树造林全球领先，我国推动野生动物繁衍生存也是逐步推进，这些都是有数据的！”

丹顶鹤：“……”

谁不会？

丹顶鹤也从杜宾手里拿出来了一沓文件，义正词严地道：

“请看！”

“我国搜救犬、导盲犬、缉毒犬数量连攀新高，它们终身都在为拯救人类而奋斗！”

道士愣了下，刚想说话。

丹顶鹤又拿出一沓：

“再看！”

“全国文旅行业新兴，动物园是一大的趋势，我们的同族兢兢业业地上班，为人类创收做出了贡献！”

道士眉心一跳，果不其然对面还有牌。

丹顶鹤从容再次伸出翅膀，桌子尽头那里有一队西服革履的小鼠，顶着文件就过来了。

“还有！”

“现在网络媒体发达！在经济下行的情况下，有诸多宠物博主走上风口，我们的同族为它们主人带来了收入，为整个人类群体都提供了就业岗位！”

“还有各种宠物交易场所，狗咖、猫咖……我们还提供了情绪价值！”

“天知道你们人类有多脆弱！”

“就这还把我们赶到山林里去？”

道士：“……”

-

与此同时，锦园。

宋郁输完液已经是十点多了，他情况还不是很好，昏昏沉沉的，手背上的针已经拔掉了。

家庭医生留下来些药物，之后就先离开了，宋峥国下楼去送客了。

卧室此刻只有一人一鸟。

宋郁没有想到今天会这么严重，他还是有些反胃，面色都很苍白。

只是伸着手，他的小鸟就在他的掌心。

“粼粼不开心？”

“早饭也没吃多少。”

少年唇角微微向上抿了下，很温和地开口问。

“告诉我。”

白粼粼闻言还愣了下，本来他是低着鸟头用爪子刨宋郁的手，打算自己先emo一会儿，毕竟人生病了，他一说对方肯定又要处理事情。

但是现在……

鸟歪头看向人。

宋郁眼眸微垂着，重复道：

“告诉我，发生了什么？”

白粼粼其实有点心动了，爪子都往前伸了一步，他就是很郁闷，被发现了……

鸟侧了下头，看门那里没什么动静，索性就化形了。

宋郁唇角微微上扬，面前多了个跨坐在他身上的“少年”，他抬手就揽住对方的腰。

侧头看着，等着“人”讲。

“我今天早上……”

嘎吱——

门开了。

宋郁掌心的温度立马消逝，被子上多了个毛绒绒的小鸡，啪嗒啪嗒地往他的方向走，一个鸟头扎进被子里，拱了拱，再次进去了。

少年微微蹙了下眉，侧眸看向门口，看到是宋峥国后才眉眼平和了起来。

“爷爷。”

老人走了过来，很关心地问：“好点了没有？”

宋郁闻言点了点头，“我没事，没有那么头晕了，您放心。”

卧室里安安静静的。

就这么过了几秒钟。

宋峥国深吸一口气，仿佛是实在忍不住了，环顾了下四周，问：

“鸟儿呢？”

宋郁其实是怔了下，甚至自动回答：

“它在睡觉。”

被子里的凸起动了下。

宋峥国：“……”

“您找它有什么事吗？”

眼看着孙子看得这么紧，宋峥国一时半会还没办法，但他其实就想和鸟儿谈一谈，并没有恶意的。

老人叹了口气，他现在也不想同孩子说他知道这事，生病了，起码是要休息一下午才行。

不过就在这时，宋峥国像是突然想起来什么，转头很和蔼地道：

“祥云阁的蟹黄包又送过来新的了，我想着鸟儿估计喜欢，它来尝尝？”

宋郁眉心一跳：

“有盐，它不能……”

被子的凸起往上顶了下。

“……”

宋峥国又道：“我想起来了，前些天你奶奶托梦，说我给了鸟儿见面礼，她也不能落人于后。”

“她早年就爱买金子，还有一套小金猪，不知道鸟儿喜欢不喜欢。”

被子的凸起顶得更高了。

“噢对了，小郁你请的那位阿姨早上又送过来一个盒子，我看里头全是些小衣服，有个还是小夹克呢……”

被子终于被顶开了。

一个毛绒绒鸟头探了出来，歪头看着老人。

鸟眼圆圆的。

真的？

宋郁：“……”

“你要去吗？困不困？”

“困可以睡觉的。”

宋郁神色平静，只是低头询问，用手指碰了碰小鸟的羽毛。

“啾啾！”

鸟啪嗒啪嗒地出来了，站到了床边，仰头看着老人。

宋郁面色沉了下来。

-

管理局这里还是在吵。

“可这里是城市，人员本就密集，除了南市本地的居民之外，还有广泛的外来务工人员，负责社会治安的相关部门压力已经很大了。再出现大量的妖怪，必然是会乱套的！”

道士仍然是坚持地站在人类的立场上，他确实是749局的激进派，妖怪这种生灵应当与人类保持距离，而不是混杂在一起。

这么不起眼的一个小巷……人来人往的。

但凡有个妖怪起了邪念，想要快速提升修为，那会不会直接吞食路边的人？

那是多大的安全隐患！

丹顶鹤也很生气，伸着翅膀就怒斥：

“什么意思？妖怪多了就乱套？时代变了好不好！你以为你们人类肉质很好吗？”

“那些攻击人类的妖怪，你去灰榜上看看，哪个不是深山老林的，它们那是纯粹没吃的。”

“城市里多的是好吃的，串串香，麻辣烫，烤冷面！我们妖怪有东西吃！”

“真给自己贴脸，城市的人类天天通勤加班，皮肉早就垮了！谁要吃！”

桌子上的小妖怪都纷纷附和，有几只还窃窃私语道：

“这个专员一看就不注重保养。”

“像个枯树。”

“就是就是！”

道士闭了闭眼，彻底没招了，不过他深吸一口气，还是问：

“你能够确切地保证城市的妖怪绝对不会攻击人类吗？”
chunks.englishText:
The old Taoist priest glanced at his phone. Unsurprisingly, there was no signal—the "Domain" here was under the demons' control.

Although Bureau 749 possessed the nominal authority to "inspect," the Demon Management Bureau had instituted a strict rule: only solitary humans were permitted to enter the base.

It was a delicate balance of power.

"Why are there more and more demons appearing lately?"

The Taoist priest spoke with a booming, robust voice, folding his arms as he delivered his interrogation. He genuinely believed something was amiss.

And what was this nonsense about the Demon Realm developing a stipend system...? How had they even pulled that off?

The Red-Crowned Crane replied neither humbly nor haughtily, "It's merely the revival of spiritual energy. Why make a fuss over nothing?"

Taoist: "..."

"Still, massing such huge numbers of demons in the city is inherently unreasonable. Demons belong back in the mountains and forests!"

Hearing this, the Red-Crowned Crane flew into a rage. He slammed a wing onto the table and proclaimed with righteous indignation, "What do you mean, 'back in the mountains and forests'? Is this world meant solely for you humans? The forests... haven't all the forests been logged to death by you lot?"

"So many of our kin are left homeless!"

Having come fully prepared, the Taoist priest pulled a stack of relevant documents from his bag and slapped them onto the table with a smack.

"Look at this!"

"Our nation's afforestation leads the world! Our initiatives to promote the breeding and survival of wildlife are advancing step by step! There are hard statistics for all of this!"

Red-Crowned Crane: "..."

*Who doesn't have documents?*

The Red-Crowned Crane promptly retrieved a thick bundle of files from the Doberman and held them up, declaring sonorously, "Take a look at *this*!"

"The number of search-and-rescue dogs, guide dogs, and drug-sniffing dogs in our country has climbed to historic highs! They dedicate their entire lives to serving humanity!"

The Taoist priest froze. Just as he opened his mouth to speak, the Crane pulled out yet another stack of papers.

"Look again!"

"The national culture and tourism sector is booming, with zoos being a major trend. Our kin work diligently day in and day out, making immense contributions to human revenue!"

The Taoist priest's brow twitched. Sure enough, the opposing side still had cards to play.

With composed elegance, the Red-Crowned Crane extended his wing once more. At the far end of the table, a team of tiny mice dressed in tailored suits marched forward, carrying documents atop their heads.

"Furthermore!"

"Online media is thriving today! Even in an economic downturn, numerous pet bloggers have caught the wind of opportunity. Our kin generate massive income for their owners and provide employment opportunities for human society as a whole!"

"Not to mention all the pet commerce venues—dog cafés, cat cafés... We even provide emotional value!"

"God knows how fragile you humans are!"

"And after all that, you want to drive us back into the wilderness?"

Taoist: "..."

-

At the same time, inside Jinyuan.

It was already past ten in the morning by the time Song Yu finished his IV infusion. His condition remained precarious; he felt dizzy and disoriented, though the needle on the back of his hand had finally been removed.

The family doctor left behind some medications and departed first, while Song Zhengguo went downstairs to see the guest out.

Only one person and one bird remained in the bedroom.

Song Yu hadn't expected his condition to be this severe today. Nausea still churned in his stomach, and his face was deathly pale.

He simply extended his hand, letting his little bird rest in his palm.

"Is Linlin unhappy?"

"You didn't eat much breakfast either."

The youth's lips twitched upward slightly as he asked in a gentle voice, "Tell me."

Bai Linlin froze upon hearing those words. Originally, he had lowered his head and scraped his claws against Song Yu's hand, intending to brood in silence for a while—after all, the human was sick, and speaking up would only force Song Yu to handle another problem.

But now...

The bird tilted his head to look at the youth.

Song Yu lowered his gaze slightly and repeated, "Tell me, what happened?"

Bai Linlin was genuinely tempted. His claws took a small step forward; he was just so frustrated about being found out...

The bird glanced toward the doorway. Sensing no movement outside, he simply transformed.

The corners of Song Yu's lips curled up into a faint smile. Suddenly, a "youth" was straddling his waist. He raised his hand and wrapped it around the other's waist, turning his head to look at him, patiently waiting for the "human" to speak.

"This morning, I..."

*Squeak—*

The door opened.

The warmth in Song Yu's palm instantly vanished. In its place, a fluffy little chick appeared on the duvet. It waddled frantically toward his side, buried its avian head into the blanket, wriggled a bit, and hid itself once more.

The youth knit his brows slightly, turning his eyes toward the doorway. His expression softened only when he saw that it was Song Zhengguo.

"Grandpa."

The old man walked over and asked with deep concern, "Are you feeling any better?"

Song Yu nodded. "I'm fine. The dizziness has subsided a bit. Don't worry."

Silence settled over the bedroom.

A few seconds passed like this.

Song Zhengguo took a deep breath, looking around the room as if he couldn't hold it back any longer. "Where is the bird?"

Song Yu blinked, answering almost automatically, "It's sleeping."

The bump under the blanket wriggled slightly.

Song Zhengguo: "..."

"Do you need something from it, Grandpa?"

Seeing how tightly his grandson guarded the little creature, Song Zhengguo realized he couldn't do much for the moment. In truth, he merely wanted to have a quiet chat with the bird, devoid of any ill intent.

The old man sighed. He didn't want to bring up his knowledge of the matter while the boy was sick; Song Yu needed to rest for at least the afternoon.

However, right at that moment, Song Zhengguo seemed to remember something. He turned around and said with a warm, benign smile, "Xiangyun Pavilion just delivered a fresh batch of crab roe buns. I thought the little bird might like them. Want to let it have a taste?"

Song Yu's brow twitched. "They contain salt. It can't—"

The bump under the blanket nudged upward.

"..."

Song Zhengguo added, "Ah, I just remembered. A few days ago, your grandmother appeared in my dream and said that since I gave the bird a welcoming gift, she shouldn't fall behind."

"She loved buying gold during her early years and left behind a set of little golden pigs. I wonder if the bird would like them."

The bump under the blanket pushed up even higher.

"Oh, right. That auntie you hired brought over another box this morning. I looked inside and saw it was full of tiny clothes—there's even a little jacket..."

The blanket was finally thrown open.

A fluffy bird head popped out, tilting to look at the old man with round, wide eyes.

*For real?*

Song Yu: "..."

"Do you want to go? Are you tired?"

"If you're sleepy, you can just sleep."

Song Yu's expression remained calm as he lowered his head to ask, lightly brushing the bird's soft feathers with his finger.

"Chirrup!"

The bird waddled out eagerly, standing at the edge of the bed and looking up at the old man.

Song Yu's face darkened completely.

-

Over at the Bureau, the argument was still raging.

"But this is a city! The population density is high enough as it is. Beside Nanshi's local residents, there's a massive influx of migrant workers. The law enforcement departments are already under immense strain. If a large number of demons flood in, it will inevitably lead to chaos!"

The Taoist priest firmly maintained his stance on behalf of humanity. He was indeed an aggressive hardliner within Bureau 749—creatures like demons ought to keep their distance from humans rather than mingling together.

Look at this inconspicuous little alleyway... people coming and going continuously.

If even a single demon nursed evil intentions and sought to rapidly elevate its cultivation, wouldn't it directly devour passersby on the street?

What a colossal security hazard that would be!

The Red-Crowned Crane was equally furious, spreading his wings and bellowing, "What are you implying? Chaos just because there are more demons? Times have changed, alright?! Do you really think human flesh tastes that good?"

"As for the demons that attack humans, go take a look at the Grey List! Which one of them isn't from the deep mountains and ancient forests? They only do it because they have literally nothing else to eat!"

"Cities are overflowing with delicious delicacies—skewered hotpot, spicy soup, grilled cold noodles! We demons have plenty of good food to eat!"

"Stop flattering yourselves! City humans commute and work overtime every single day; their flesh and skin are long ruined and flabby! Who would want to eat that?!"

The little demons gathered on the table voiced their agreement one after another. A few even whispered among themselves:

"This specialist clearly doesn't invest in skin care."

"He looks like a withered tree."

"Exactly, exactly!"

The Taoist priest closed his eyes, completely at a loss. Taking a deep breath, he asked solemnly, "Can you definitively guarantee that demons in the city will *never* attack humans?"

chunks.chineseText:
丹顶鹤觉得这简直就是在侮辱它们，很认真地道：

“城市里的妖怪，绝大多数是小型的，它们有的从出生起就是待在它们的监护人身边的，最早接触的不是人类的恶意，而是那种全然的照顾和爱。”

“我们怎么可能去攻击监护人的同族？”

道士愣了下。

丹顶鹤直接起身了，伸着翅膀就示意这个“专员”跟他来，很快它们就抵达了大厅东南角的“历史回廊”。

“中央一开始就给我们下了指示，说要强化历史教育，妖怪和人的相处时间本就很长，从古至今都有纷争，好不容易现在出现了稳定的局面，我们一定要维持好。”

“所以你看，我们还修建了纪念墙。”

丹顶鹤很是从容自信地介绍道，还伸翅膀指了指照片下面的注释，很专业地道：

“这里有照片的信息，南市管理局成立于九十年代，那个时候还很没有组织……”

道士在后面看着，说不震惊是假的，他没有想到这群妖怪居然弄得像模像样的，这学了不少人类的吧？

老头微微后仰，面色其实已经有了欣赏之意。

成。

还不错。

但就在这时。

丹顶鹤指着一幅巨大的红底合影道：

“你看，这是我们首位监护人亲自前来为他的小鸟注册登记，这实在是具有历史意义的一幕！”

“像这样的人类，我们妖界是非常欢迎的！”

道士抬眼看了过去，一秒，两秒……

他僵住了。

这不是，峥国的孙子吗？

旁边……是只巨鸟？

-

鸟这会儿已经高高兴兴地跟着老人出来了，啪嗒啪嗒地在地板上走着。

白粼粼其实已经衡量过了，既然瞒不下去了，那就不瞒了，反正宋郁那个时候他就装不下去。

说不准……

宋郁接受度高是继承了爷爷？

鸟在后面走着，用翅膀托了下鸟头，沉思。

不过也没有关系。

宋郁肯定站在他这一边的！

鸟又鼓起了信心，大摇大摆地跟在后面。

书房里鲜香四溢。

宋峥国说到做到，出高价半路截胡了祥云阁的外送，蟹黄包还冒着热气。

与此同时，他也从三楼储藏室拿下来一个黑匣子，打开了，里面是一个圆滚滚的金猪。

至于楼下那套小衣服，当然也是带了上来，很时尚的小夹克，阿姨还做了内衬的。

白粼粼一开始还吃得很开心，后面就有点默默心虚了，伸爪子后退了几步。

真奇怪，不确定真假的时候，希望是真的。

但确定都是实打实的之后，他又有点退缩。

“鸟儿，我没有恶意。”

宋峥国很诚恳地道。

“小郁这孩子，其实没有得到过太多的爱，他父母不尽责，我也何尝不是？我工作繁忙，即使是带着他，也很难抽出来时间去陪伴。”

“他自己在空旷的房子里住了很久。”

老人不知道怎么解释，他只是道：

“谢谢你，鸟儿。”

白粼粼爪子并了并，其实觉得有点不敢当，他自从来了宋家，吃得珠圆玉润的。

当鸟当得忘我了。

很爽的。

但对面的老人还在继续，面容都很宽和，只是娓娓道来一件事：

“爷爷以前从军的时候，遇见一件事，那个时候是冬天，东北的雪厚得到膝盖，当时啊，条件艰苦，没有那么多的棉衣，人都冻得麻木，脚步也不自觉地慢了下来……”

“但这其实很危险的，我掉队了，冰天雪地的，白茫茫一片，天色也暗了，只有那黑色的松林……”

白粼粼听得有些入神，啪嗒啪嗒地走了过去，仰头看着老人。

“啾啾！”

[然后呢？]

宋峥国闻言笑了下，回想起来那段奇妙的经历，只是道：

“有一头鹿走了过来，它的角是泛着金光的，我几乎没了知觉，但是它一靠近……周身却暖和了起来。”

“后面意识都变得模糊不清了，隐约觉得是一位男童，在牵着我的手走……直到我再醒过来，身边就已经围着我的战友了……”

白粼粼觉得好神奇，居然还会引路，他也忘了自己也是妖怪这件事了，只是仰头又催促道：

“啾啾！”

[继续继续！]

宋峥国的语气变得很平和，“同战友们讲他们是不信的，因为在他们的眼里，我是自己走过来的。”

“后来我去当地的猎户那里问过，他们管这种生灵叫做……”

“山神。”

-

管理局内。

丹顶鹤本来相当骄傲地介绍了这副图片，但是那位“专员”似乎大为震惊，只是反复地向它确认247的监护人姓名。

它只能指了指照片下面。

这不是写着么？

[宋郁]

道士闭了闭眼，不愿面对现实，后面老头只是伸出来一根手指，提要求道：

“我需要查一下这个妖怪的档案。”

丹顶鹤虽然有些不解，但还是很有自信的，查就查！

它们管理局的每一个妖怪都是好的！

不过就在这时，身后传来一句悠悠的叹息：

“究竟是谁教你们这么拍照的……还是红底……”

-

后面查档的时候其实是有点不顺利的，因为道士提出了一点疑问：

“它在七月的时候，妖力登记还是F级。”

“怎么八月末就直接到A级？这合规吗？”

丹顶鹤：“……”

它就知道247迟早会给它闯出祸事来。

走歪门邪道。

“是不是吃人了！”

道士表情很是严肃，觉得相当有问题，尤其是这只妖怪，应该……还在老友的家里。

丹顶鹤闭了闭眼，只是解释道：

“不是，它一个F级的鸟，啃人的手指都费劲，这是它用其他妖怪的妖力津贴快速提上去的……”

道士这下可算找到问题了，直接质问：

“妖力津贴不是只能一妖一用吗？这怎么还可以叠加使用？”

“绝对有问题！”

“这个编号247的，必须要转移至749局检查。”

丹顶鹤这就怒了，一翅膀拍桌子，道：

“你摆什么谱！”

“它没有问题就是没有问题！不信我就跟你一起去，它现在也就八个月大，一岁还不到，能吃你的手指头啊！”

道士正有此意：

“去就去！”

-

锦园这里一片祥和。

白粼粼后面试探着化形了，站在书房里，面色有些茫然，后面只是道：

“我其实什么也不会。”

“现在只学会了化形。”

宋峥国笑着道：

“叫我爷爷就好。”

鸟不好意思，背了背手。

“这样的话，那倒是的确可以给鸟儿买金镯子了。”

白粼粼垂着头，面色有些泛红，挺不好意思的，他也就展示了一会儿，立马又变成一只圆滚滚的小鸟。

不过就在这时，楼下有急促的拍门声。

宋峥国蹙了蹙眉，起身准备去看看情况，鸟也没别的事，扑棱翅膀站到人的肩膀上了。

大约一分钟后。

打开了玄关的大门。
chunks.englishText:
The Red-Crowned Crane felt that this question was an outright insult to their kind. He stated with utmost gravity, "The vast majority of demons in the city are small ones. Some have stayed beside their human guardians since birth. The first thing they encountered wasn't human malice, but total care and love."

"Why on earth would we attack the kin of our own guardians?"

The Taoist priest was stunned.

The Red-Crowned Crane stood up and motioned with a spread wing for the "specialist" to follow him. Soon, they arrived at the "Corridor of History" located in the southeastern corner of the grand hall.

"The central authority issued instructions from the very beginning, emphasizing the need to strengthen historical education. Demons and humans have coexisted for a long time, enduring conflicts from ancient times to the present. Now that we've finally established a stable situation, we must preserve it at all costs."

"So you see, we even constructed a memorial wall."

The Red-Crowned Crane introduced the area with calm confidence, pointing a wing toward the caption beneath a photograph as he explained professionally, "Here is the information for this photo. The Nanshi Bureau was established in the 1990s, back when things were still quite disorganized..."

The Taoist priest observed from behind, his shock far from fake. He had never expected this group of demons to organize things so impeccably. They must have learned a great deal from humans, hadn't they?

The old man leaned back slightly, a look of genuine appreciation surfacing on his face.

*Fine.*

*Not bad at all.*

Just then, the Red-Crowned Crane pointed to a massive group photo set against a red background.

"Look! This is our very first guardian personally coming here to register his little bird! This was truly an event of monumental historical significance!"

"We in the Demon Realm welcome humans like him with open arms!"

The Taoist priest raised his eyes to look. One second, two seconds...

He froze completely.

Isn't that... Zhengguo's grandson?!

And beside him... was a giant bird?!

-

Meanwhile, the bird had already happily followed the old man out of the bedroom, waddling across the hardwood floor.

Bai Linlin had already weighed the situation. Since the cat was out of the bag, there was no point in hiding anymore. Besides, he hadn't been able to keep up the act in front of Song Yu back then anyway.

Who knows...

Maybe Song Yu's high acceptance level was inherited from his grandfather?

Walking behind the old man, the bird cupped his head with his wings, lost in deep thought.

Not that it mattered!

Song Yu would definitely take his side!

Rebooting his confidence, the bird strutted grandly behind the old man.

Inside the study, a rich, savory aroma filled the air. Song Zhengguo was a man of his word—he had paid a high price to intercept Xiangyun Pavilion's delivery midway, and the crab roe buns were still steaming hot.

At the same time, he retrieved a black wooden box from the third-floor storage room. When opened, it revealed a plump, golden pig figurine inside.

As for the set of tiny clothes from downstairs, they had naturally been brought up as well—a stylish little jacket complete with a custom lining made by the auntie.

At first, Bai Linlin ate with absolute joy, but gradually, a quiet guilt crept over him. He pulled back his claws and took a few steps back.

It was a strange feeling: when he hadn't been sure if it was real, he had wished it were true.

Now that he confirmed everything was genuine and tangible, he felt like retreating instead.

"Little bird, I mean no harm," Song Zhengguo said with profound sincerity.

"Little Yu... he didn't receive much love growing up. His parents failed in their duties, and I was no better. I was consumed by my work, and even when I had him by my side, I could rarely spare the time to keep him company."

"He lived in a vast, empty house by himself for a very long time."

The old man didn't quite know how to explain it all, concluding simply, "Thank you, little bird."

Bai Linlin pulled his claws together, feeling a bit unworthy of such gratitude. Ever since coming to the Song household, he had been fed until he was plump and sleek.

He had been enjoying his life as a bird far too much.

It was honestly glorious.

The old man opposite him continued speaking, his countenance full of gentleness as he recounted a tale from the past:

"Back when I served in the military, I encountered something extraordinary. It was winter, and the snow in the Northeast was knee-deep. Conditions were harsh back then—we didn't have enough padded coats, so people grew numb from the cold, their footsteps slowing down involuntarily..."

"That was actually extremely dangerous. I fell behind the troop. In that endless expanse of ice and snow, everything was a blinding white, and the sky was darkening. There was nothing but the black pine forest..."

Bai Linlin listened intently, waddling closer and tilting his head up at the old man.

"Chirrup!"

*[And then?]*

Song Zhengguo smiled faintly at the sound, recalling that miraculous encounter. "A deer walked out. Its antlers glowed with a soft golden light. I had virtually lost all sensation, but the moment it drew close... warmth enveloped my entire body."

"My consciousness blurred after that. I vaguely felt a young boy holding my hand, leading me forward... By the time I woke up again, my comrades were already gathered around me..."

Bai Linlin thought it sounded magical—a creature that could guide lost people! He completely forgot that he himself was a demon too, looking up and urging the old man on:

"Chirrup! Chirrup!"

*[Keep going, keep going!]*

Song Zhengguo's tone turned serene. "My comrades didn't believe me when I told them, because in their eyes, I had walked back all by myself."

"Later, I asked the local hunters about it. They called such creatures..."

"Mountain Gods."

-

Inside the Bureau.

The Red-Crowned Crane had been proudly introducing the photograph, but the "specialist" appeared profoundly shocked, repeatedly confirming the guardian's name for Number 247.

The Crane had no choice but to point at the bottom of the frame.

Wasn't it written right there?

[Song Yu]

The Taoist priest closed his eyes, unwilling to face reality. Finally, the old man held up a single finger and demanded, "I need to inspect this demon's file."

Although somewhat puzzled, the Red-Crowned Crane remained full of confidence. *Inspect away!*

Every single demon in their Bureau was a good citizen!

Just then, a faint, leisurely sigh echoed from behind:

"Who on earth taught you to take photos like this... using a red background, no less..."

-

The file inspection didn't go quite smoothly, as the Taoist priest raised a sharp objection:

"Back in July, its demonic energy registration was listed as F-rank."

"How did it suddenly jump straight to A-rank by late August? Is this compliant with regulations?!"

Red-Crowned Crane: "..."

He *knew* Number 247 would bring trouble sooner or later!

Taking crooked shortcuts!

"Did it devour a human?!"

The Taoist priest's expression turned grimly serious. He felt something was gravely wrong—especially since this demon was likely... still inside his old friend's home!

The Red-Crowned Crane closed his eyes and explained, "No! It's an F-rank bird! It would struggle to even nibble through a human finger! It raised its rank quickly by using demonic energy stipends transferred from other demons..."

The Taoist priest finally caught hold of a flaw and interrogated immediately, "Aren't demonic energy stipends strictly restricted to one per demon? How can they be stacked and used like this?"

"There is definitely something wrong here!"

"Subject Number 247 must be transferred to Bureau 749 for examination immediately!"

The Red-Crowned Crane blew his top, slamming a wing onto the desk. "Who are you to put on airs with me?!"

"When I say it has no issues, it has no issues! If you don't believe me, I'll go with you! It's barely eight months old—not even a year! What could it possibly bite off from your finger?!"

The Taoist priest declared firmly, "Then let's go right now!"

-

Inside Jinyuan, peace prevailed.

Bai Linlin tentatively tried transforming into his human form. Standing in the study with a bewildered expression, he whispered softly, "I actually don't know how to do anything."

"Right now, I've only learned how to transform."

Song Zhengguo smiled warmly. "Just call me Grandpa."

Shy, the bird tucked his hands behind his back.

"In that case, it seems I really should buy a golden bracelet for our little bird."

Bai Linlin hung his head, his cheeks flushing pink with embarrassment. He only maintained the form for a brief moment before instantly reverting back into a plump little bird.

Right at that moment, frantic pounding echoed from the front door downstairs.

Song Zhengguo knit his brows and stood up to check on the situation. Having nothing else to do, the little bird fluttered his wings and perched atop the old man's shoulder.

Roughly a minute later...

The front door at the entryway was pulled open.

chunks.chineseText:
外面站着一个奇装异服的道士，以及一个系着藏蓝色丝带的女士，两个人均是臭脸。

“平云？”

宋峥国其实是有些意外的，怎么不说一声就……

道士一眼就看到了老友肩头的鸟，大声地道：

“小妖！”

或许是过于直白，白粼粼直接愣住了，对方抬手就要过来拿他。

鸟直接扑棱翅膀飞走了，站在不远处的地板上，有些懵懵的。

什么情况？

这个时候旁边那位系着丝带的女士抬手就是一拍，硬生生把那个道士的胳膊弄到了玄关的墙壁上，木板都裂开了点。

丹顶鹤不满道：

“干什么呢！它才八个月！”

道士着急地同宋峥国解释：“峥国，这东西是个妖怪，小郁肯定是被他哄骗了！”

“我今天一定要帮你处理了！”

丹顶鹤真是要气死了。

“你再说！”

眼看一人一鹤要掐起来。

并且已经进门了。

白粼粼头脑风暴中，立即开始装傻，鸟眼均匀地往外瞥，翅膀半伸着，爪子也一瘸一拐的。

“啾……啾啾……”

好一个智障小鸟。

门口这会儿的动静也停了，道士蹙眉看了过来，有点嫌弃道：

“这是个笨的？”

不过就在这时，楼上有门开合的动静，有一道很冷的声音传了过来：

“为什么围着我的小鸟？”

玄关那处更安静了。

“粼粼，过来。”

Standing outside was an strangely attired Taoist priest alongside a lady wearing a dark blue ribbon. Both of them wore foul expressions.

"Pingyun?"

Song Zhengguo was genuinely taken aback. Why had his old friend arrived without giving any prior notice...?

The Taoist priest's eyes instantly locked onto the bird perched on his friend's shoulder, and he shouted loudly, "Demonic beast!"

Perhaps his reaction was too blunt and direct, leaving Bai Linlin utterly stunned. The priest raised his hand, reaching out to grab him.

The bird frantically flapped his wings and flew off, landing on the floor a short distance away, looking completely dazed.

*What is going on here?*

Right then, the lady wearing the ribbon raised her hand and delivered a sharp slap, slamming the Taoist priest's arm hard against the entryway wall. The wooden paneling even cracked slightly.

The Red-Crowned Crane barked in displeasure, "What do you think you're doing?! It's only eight months old!"

The Taoist priest anxiously tried to explain to Song Zhengguo, "Zhengguo, this creature is a demon! Little Yu must have been tricked by it!"

"I am definitely going to dispose of it for you today!"

The Red-Crowned Crane was furious. "Say that one more time!"

Seeing that the human and the crane were about to engage in a physical brawl—and had already stepped inside the house—Bai Linlin's brain went into overdrive. He immediately decided to play dumb: his bird eyes rolled outward in a dim-witted stare, one wing hung half-extended, and he limped on one leg.

"Chirup... chirup..."

What a flawless impression of a foolish, dim-witted little bird!

The commotion at the doorway ground to a halt. The Taoist priest knit his brows as he looked over, a trace of disgust in his voice. "Is this one... an idiot?"

Just then, the sound of a door opening echoed from upstairs, followed by a cold, icy voice carrying down the stairwell:

"Why are you crowding around my little bird?"

The entryway fell dead silent.

"Linlin, come here."

***

chunks.chineseText:
第41章

地板上的蓝羽小鸟本来还是保持一个奇形怪状的站姿的，但是一听到楼上的声音后立马仰着鸟头看过去了。

人！

白粼粼直接一个扭头起飞，扑棱翅膀还有点着急，爪子都在地板上打了个滑，但最终顺顺利利地抵达宋郁的肩头。

挺胸抬头。

楼下的两人一鹤看后都是一阵沉默，道士尤为生气，觉得自己被欺骗了，伸着手就对宋峥国道：

“你看看你看看！这小妖鬼精鬼精的！”

宋郁面色冷白，抬步直接走下来了，尽管精神还是有些不济，但在玄关口的时候直直地盯着那个穿着道袍的人，面无表情的。

道士：“……”

宋峥国见状连忙道：“小郁，这位是爷爷的朋友，”

道士见状也是松开了和丹顶鹤的纠缠的手，整理了下自己的衣冠，站好了。

多少年没见过了。

“摆什么谱？切。”

门口的那位“女士”环着手臂就冷哼了一声。

宋郁抬眼看了过去，感觉有些熟悉的气质，但又辨别不出来。

“这位……爷爷也不知道。”

宋峥国其实也觉得棘手，毕竟一开门，对面这两个人就在吵，连介绍环节都没有，在玄关口就干起来了。

老人看了下自家的门框。

居然已经裂开了。

宋峥国只是觉得荒谬，这位“女士”……她这么力大无穷？

丹顶鹤在门口站着，心道监护人认不出来就算了，247总不能认不出来吧？

好歹也是个A级妖怪了。

但是它等了好一会，甚至还特地给了宋郁肩头那只一个眼神，上下扫视了下，咳嗽一声，然后再撇开视线。

丹顶鹤认为这再明显不过了。

然而，少年肩头的那只圆滚滚的蓝羽小鸟只是一个劲地歪头看，爪子还活动了下，仿佛是觉得看不太清楚，试图往前凑一凑鸟头，但一个重心不稳，开始一顿扑棱翅膀。

“……”

最后还是宋郁抬手给接住了。

蓝羽小鸟这才重新回了原来位置，收了收翅膀，假装一切事情都没发生。

玄关这里保持着沉默。

丹顶鹤闭了闭眼，深吸一口气，它就知道不能对247抱有任何希望。

于是抬手伸了过去。

它的掌心金纹涌动，在双方面对面的空间里形成了一道“墙”，透明的，但这些宋峥国看不到，丹顶鹤有意避开了。

至于宋郁和肩头的某只，则是在短暂的晃眼之后，看清楚了对面的真实情况。

一个道士，一个……脖子伸得很长的丹顶鹤。

宋郁觉得自己真是烧得不轻。

“啾啾！”

肩头上的小鸟叫声微微唤醒了他，人这才反应过来，是管理局的丹顶鹤。

不过想到这里，宋郁蹙了蹙眉。

怎么，要家访？

他的小鸟最近表现很好的。

“小郁认识吗？”

最后还是宋峥国又问了一句，打破了玄关这里死一般的沉寂。

对面的道士闻言也眯了眯眼，耐心地等着，不过少年没有任何犹豫，只是很平静地道：

“爷爷，这是我的朋友。”

肩头上的小鸟毛绒绒的，很自然地用头拱了拱人的下巴。

“啾！”

-

最后成功地进了门。

不过是分成两组，道士坚持要和宋郁单独谈谈，丹顶鹤则是看中了宋峥国这个老头子。

白粼粼夹在中间窝窝囊囊的，最后还是丹顶鹤挥了挥手，很嫌弃地道：

“跟着你监护人吧。”

鸟如愿以偿地上了宋郁的肩头。

地点分别是一楼的茶室与二楼的书房。

宋峥国听到“监护人”这三个字其实愣了下，心里再三思考，最终还是不得不承认……那可能是说的是小郁。

丹顶鹤优雅地道：“走吧，我们聊聊。”

最终老人选择的地点是茶室，他拉开门，让那位“女士”进来，顺带给沏了一杯热茶。

丹顶鹤端坐在红木椅子上，抬手抿了一口，随后看向这个老头子。

监护人的长辈。

247现在的身份已经趋近于暴露了。

它眯了眯眼，索性直接问道：

“是这样，你觉得那个臭道士说的话是真的吗？”

宋峥国：“……”

他已经见过了，这否认也似乎没有意义，老人皱了皱眉，只是也拿起一杯茶，转而反问道：

“你同鸟儿认识？”

丹顶鹤心想这不废话，它思考了一下，直接变回了本体，用翅膀托着那杯冒着热气的茶，很优雅地整理了下自己脖子上的丝巾。

看向对面的老人。

很矜贵的样子。

宋峥国甚至刚喝完一口茶，一抬眼直接愣住了，整个人的大脑皮层都变得光滑，最后直接呛住了，开始一个劲地咳嗽。

“咳咳咳……不、不好意思。”

老头儿侧头拿了纸巾，对着椅子旁边的一只鹤道歉。

宋峥国其实对于家养的鸟儿确实接受度高些，一来鸟儿本体就很可爱，毛绒绒的，还会穿小披风……就算是化形了，看着也还是个孩子模样。

而面前的……是鹤。

“没关系，人类是有些大惊小怪的。”

丹顶鹤仍然端庄，拿起茶杯又浅浅地啜饮了一口。

鸟类的羽毛就是最好看的部分，人类为此而感到惊艳再正常不过，它可以给这位监护人的长辈一些时间适应。

宋峥国咳嗽了一会，深呼吸一口，然后闭了闭眼，再次回头看了下，那只一米六高的大型涉禽还在坐着，脖子上系着人类的丝带。

它注意到了目光还看了过来，一幅宽容怜悯的样子。

没见识的人类。

宋峥国重新转回了头，再度闭眼，没事的，没事的。

不过是一只会说人话的国家一级保护动物而已。

而已……

-

与此同时。

宋郁已经去了书房，很客气地先开了门，他肩头的小鸟从头到尾都是紧紧贴着他的脖子的，羽毛很是蓬松，成为一个毛球了。

它吓到了。

这位道士跨着四方步走了进来，甚至都还没有坐下，就想回过头来说教，但是被打断了——

“您贵姓？”

宋郁抬手关上了门，出声问道，语气平直且没有起伏，只是很客气地询问。

“……叫我李爷爷就行。”

道士其实也是有些慨叹，当年见到这孩子的时候还那么小，现在居然长这么高了。

就是看着有点脾气不好。

干巴巴的老头摇了摇头。

宋郁身高已经将近一米八五，再加上前些日子健身，肩宽背直的，那张偏冷的脸直接褪去了些“青涩感”，取而代之的是一种密不透风的压迫。

“您先坐。”

这道声音疏离又很寡淡。

道士闻言收了收袖子，的确拉开椅子坐下了，见到对面这孩子也入座了，这才开始单刀直入地道：

“你这小鸟，它是个妖怪！”

宋郁闻言一顿，随即抬眼看了过来，扯唇笑了下，很是不在意道：

“那又如何？”

-

一楼茶室。

丹顶鹤端坐在椅子上，翅膀托着茶杯，观察了下旁边的人类，开始娓娓道来：

Chapter 41 (Part 1)

The little blue-feathered bird on the floor had originally been frozen in a bizarre, contorted stance, but the moment it heard the voice from upstairs, it instantly snapped its head up to look.

A human!

Bai Linlin spun around and took off, flapping his wings in an anxious flurry. His claws even skidded on the hardwood floor, but he managed to land smoothly on Song Yu’s shoulder in the end.

Chest puffed, head held high.

Downstairs, the two humans and the crane fell into a brief, stunned silence. The Taoist priest was particularly incensed, feeling thoroughly duped. He pointed an accusatory finger at Song Yu and barked to Song Zhenguo:

“Look at that! Just look at that! That little demon is as sly as a fox!”

Song Yu’s face was cool and pale. He stepped down the stairs, and despite his lingering fever and weak constitution, he stared straight at the robe-clad man standing in the entryway, his face completely devoid of expression.

The Taoist priest: “…”

Seeing the tension, Song Zhenguo hurried to intervene. “Xiao Yu, this is an old friend of your grandfather.”

Hearing this, the priest finally released his hold on the red-crowned crane, straightened his robes, and stood upright.

It had been so many years since they last met.

“What airs are you putting on? Hmph.”

The “lady” standing by the front door crossed her arms and let out a cold sneer.

Song Yu raised his eyes to look over. Something about her felt strangely familiar, yet he couldn’t quite put his finger on it.

“As for this one… Grandpa doesn’t know either.”

Song Zhenguo actually found the situation quite tricky. After all, the moment he opened the front door, the two of them were already at each other’s throats. Without even a word of introduction, they had started brawling right in the foyer.

The old man cast a glance at his front doorframe.

It was actually cracked.

Song Zhenguo found it utterly absurd—was this “lady”… really that ridiculously strong?

Standing at the doorway, the crane thought to itself: *So what if his guardian can’t recognize me? Surely 247 shouldn’t be this blind, right? He’s an A-rank demon now, for goodness’ sake!*

It waited for a long moment, even going out of its way to shoot a meaningful glare at the bird on Song Yu’s shoulder. It scanned the little bird up and down, let out a deliberate cough, and then averted its gaze.

The crane felt that hint couldn't possibly be any clearer.

However, the round, fluffy blue bird on the young man’s shoulder merely tilted its head back and forth, shifting its tiny feet as if it couldn't see clearly. It attempted to lean its head farther forward to get a better look, only to lose its balance and begin flapping its wings wildly in panic.

“…”

In the end, Song Yu reached up and caught the clumsy bird in his hand.

Only then did the little blue bird return to its spot, tucking in its wings and pretending as though nothing embarrassing had just transpired.

Silence reigned over the foyer.

The crane closed its eyes and took a deep, long breath. It knew better than to hold out any hope for 247.

It raised a hand and waved it through the air.

Golden runes surged across its palm, forming an invisible "wall" in the air between the two sides. It was completely transparent, though the crane intentionally shielded it from Song Zhenguo's sight.

As for Song Yu and the creature on his shoulder, after a brief moment of blurred vision, they finally saw the true reality before them.

A Taoist priest, and… a red-crowned crane with a ridiculously stretched-out neck.

Song Yu thought his fever must be worse than he realized.

“Chirp chirp!”

The soft chirping on his shoulder gently pulled him back to reality. Only then did he realize that this was the red-crowned crane from the Bureau.

At the thought, Song Yu knit his brows slightly.

What was this? A home visit?

His little bird had been behaving exceptionally well lately.

“Xiao Yu, do you know them?”

Song Zhenguo spoke up once more, breaking the deathly silence in the foyer.

Opposite them, the Taoist priest narrowed his eyes and waited patiently. Yet, without a single moment of hesitation, the young man calmly replied:

“Grandpa, these are my friends.”

The fluffy little bird on his shoulder naturally rubbed its head against the young man’s chin.

“Chirp!”

-

In the end, the guests successfully made it past the front door.

However, they split into two separate groups. The Taoist priest insisted on having a private conversation with Song Yu, while the red-crowned crane set its sights on the old man, Song Zhenguo.

Bai Linlin was caught in the middle, looking completely helpless and pitiful. Finally, the crane waved a wing and said with utter disdain:

“Go with your guardian then.”

As requested, the bird happily returned to Song Yu’s shoulder.

The chosen locations were the tea room on the first floor and the study on the second floor.

When Song Zhenguo heard the word "guardian," he froze for a moment. After mulling it over in his mind several times, he ultimately had to accept that… it was likely referring to Xiao Yu.

The crane said gracefully, “Shall we? Let us have a chat.”

In the end, the old man chose the tea room. He pulled open the door, ushered the “lady” inside, and brewed a cup of hot tea for her.

The crane sat poised and upright on a mahogany chair. It raised a hand to take a delicate sip, then turned its gaze toward the old man.

The guardian’s elder.

247’s secret identity was now practically blown.

Narrowing its eyes, the crane decided to cut straight to the chase:

“Tell me, do you really believe the nonsensical drivel that stinky old Taoist spat out?”

Song Zhenguo: “…”

Having already witnessed the impossible with his own eyes, denying it felt completely pointless. The old man knit his brows, picked up a cup of tea, and countered with a question of his own:

“Do you know the bird?”

*Isn't that obvious?* the crane thought. After a moment of consideration, it dropped its human disguise and reverted directly to its true form. Holding the steaming cup of tea with its wing, it gracefully adjusted the silk scarf tied around its long neck.

It then looked across at the old man.

It oozed an aura of noble refinement.

Song Zhenguo had just taken a sip of tea. When he raised his eyes, he froze instantly. His brain seemed to go completely smooth for a second, and he ended up choking on his tea, coughing uncontrollably.

“Cough, cough, cough… M-my apologies.”

The old man turned his head away, grabbed a tissue, and apologized to a crane sitting beside his chair.

Truth be told, Song Zhenguo was actually quite open-minded when it came to domestic birds. For one, the bird's original form was undeniably adorable—fluffy and cute, even wearing little capes… Even when transformed into human form, it still looked like a young child.

But the creature before him now… was a full-grown crane.

“Think nothing of it. It is only natural for humans to be easily startled.”
